1.61.s:
sūta uvāca
kṣetrāṇyetāni sarvāṇi ātapanti gabhastibhiḥ
teṣāṃ kṣetrāṇyathādatte sūryo nakṣatratārakāḥ //
1.61.d:
सूत उवाच
क्षेत्राण्येतानि सर्वाणि आतपन्ति गभस्तिभिः
तेषां क्षेत्राण्यथादत्ते सूर्यो नक्षत्रतारकाः ॥
1.61.m: Sūta said: / All these fields shine with their rays; / then the Sun takes back the fields of those lunar asterisms and stars.

1.61.s:
cīrṇena sukṛteneha sukṛtānte grahāśrayāḥ
tāraṇāttārakā hyetāḥ śuklatvāccaiva tārakāḥ //
1.61.d:
चीर्णेन सुकृतेनेह सुकृतान्ते ग्रहाश्रयाः
तारणात्तारका ह्येताः शुक्लत्वाच्चैव तारकाः ॥
1.61.m: By virtue of good deeds performed here, at the end of the good deeds they have planets as their abodes. / Indeed, they are called tārakās (stars) because of carrying across (tāraṇa) and because of their whiteness (śuklatva).

1.61.s:
divyānāṃ pārthivānāṃ ca naiśānāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ
ādānānnityamādityas tejasāṃ tamasāmapi //
1.61.d:
दिव्यानां पार्थिवानां च नैशानां चैव सर्वशः
आदानान्नित्यमादित्यस् तेजसां तमसामपि ॥
1.61.m: Because he continually draws in (ādāna) heavenly, earthly, and nocturnal / splendors and darknesses from every direction, he is called Āditya.

1.61.s:
savane syandane 'rthe ca dhātur eṣa vibhāṣyate
savanāttejaso 'pāṃ ca tenāsau savitā mataḥ //
1.61.d:
सवने स्यन्दने ऽर्थे च धातुर् एष विभाष्यते
सवनात्तेजसो ऽपां च तेनासौ सविता मतः ॥
1.61.m: This verbal root is spoken in the sense of pressing out (savana) and flowing; / because of pressing forth light and water, he is regarded as Savitṛ.

1.61.s:
bahulaścandra ityeṣa hlādane dhāturucyate
śuklatve cāmṛtatve ca śītatve ca vibhāvyate //
1.61.d:
बहुलश्चन्द्र इत्येष ह्लादने धातुरुच्यते
शुक्लत्वे चामृतत्वे च शीतत्वे च विभाव्यते ॥
1.61.m: The root candr- is said to mean “to gladden” abundantly; / it is conceived in terms of whiteness, ambrosia, and coolness.

1.61.s:
sūryācandramasordivye maṇḍale bhāsvare khage
jalatejomaye śukle vṛttakuṃbhanibhe śubhe //
1.61.d:
सूर्याचन्द्रमसोर्दिव्ये मण्डले भास्वरे खगे
जलतेजोमये शुक्ले वृत्तकुंभनिभे शुभे ॥
1.61.m: The divine, luminous discs of the Sun and Moon, moving in the sky, / consist of water and fire, are white, auspicious, and resemble round jars.

1.61.s:
ghanatoyātmakaṃ tatra maṇḍalaṃ śaśinaḥ smṛtam
ghanatejomayaṃ śuklaṃ maṇḍalaṃ bhāskarasya tu //
1.61.d:
घनतोयात्मकं तत्र मण्डलं शशिनः स्मृतम्
घनतेजोमयं शुक्लं मण्डलं भास्करस्य तु ॥
1.61.m: Among them, the disc of the Moon is remembered as consisting of dense water; / the disc of the Sun, however, is white and consists of dense fire.

1.61.s:
vasanti sarvadevāś ca sthānānyetāni sarvaśaḥ
manvantareṣu sarveṣu ṛkṣasūryagrahāśrayāḥ //
1.61.d:
वसन्ति सर्वदेवाश् च स्थानान्येतानि सर्वशः
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु ऋक्षसूर्यग्रहाश्रयाः ॥
1.61.m: All the gods dwell in these abodes in every way, / residing in the lunar asterisms, the Sun, and the planets through all the manvantaras.

1.61.s:
tena grahā gṛhāṇyeva tadākhyāste bhavanti ca
sauraṃ sūryo 'viśatsthānaṃ saumyaṃ somastathaiva ca //
1.61.d:
तेन ग्रहा गृहाण्येव तदाख्यास्ते भवन्ति च
सौरं सूर्यो ऽविशत्स्थानं सौम्यं सोमस्तथैव च ॥
1.61.m: Therefore the planets (graha) are indeed houses (gṛha), and they bear those names. / The Sun entered the solar abode, and the Moon entered the lunar abode;

1.61.s:
śaukraṃ śukro 'viśatsthānaṃ ṣoḍaśārciḥ pratāpavān
bṛhad bṛhaspatiścaiva lohitaścaiva lohitam //
1.61.d:
शौक्रं शुक्रो ऽविशत्स्थानं षोडशार्चिः प्रतापवान्
बृहद् बृहस्पतिश्चैव लोहितश्चैव लोहितम् ॥
1.61.m: Venus, sixteen-rayed and powerful, entered the abode of Venus; / Jupiter entered the great (bṛhat) abode, and Mars (Lohita) entered the red (lohita) abode;

1.61.s:
śanaiścaraṃ tathā sthānaṃ devaścāpi śanaiścaraḥ
baudhaṃ budhastu svarbhānuḥ svarbhānusthānamāśritaḥ //
1.61.d:
शनैश्चरं तथा स्थानं देवश्चापि शनैश्चरः
बौधं बुधस्तु स्वर्भानुः स्वर्भानुस्थानमाश्रितः ॥
1.61.m: the god Saturn entered the abode of Saturn; / Mercury entered the mercurial abode, and Svarbhānu (Rāhu) resorted to Svarbhānu’s abode.

1.61.s:
nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvāṇi nakṣatrāṇi viśanti ca
gṛhāṇyetāni sarvāṇi jyotīṃṣi sukṛtātmanām //
1.61.d:
नक्षत्राणि च सर्वाणि नक्षत्राणि विशन्ति च
गृहाण्येतानि सर्वाणि ज्योतींषि सुकृतात्मनाम् ॥
1.61.m: And all the lunar asterisms enter into the nakṣatras. / All these celestial bodies are houses for those of virtuous souls.

1.61.s:
kalpādau sampravṛttāni nirmitāni svayaṃbhuvā
sthānānyetāni tiṣṭhanti yāvad ābhūtasaṃplavam //
1.61.d:
कल्पादौ सम्प्रवृत्तानि निर्मितानि स्वयंभुवा
स्थानान्येतानि तिष्ठन्ति यावद् आभूतसंप्लवम् ॥
1.61.m: Initiated at the beginning of the kalpa, created by the Self-born, / these abodes remain until the cosmic dissolution.

1.61.s:
manvantareṣu sarveṣu devasthānāni tāni vai
abhimānino 'vatiṣṭhante devāḥ sthānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ //
1.61.d:
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु देवस्थानानि तानि वै
अभिमानिनो ऽवतिष्ठन्ते देवाः स्थानं पुनः पुनः ॥
1.61.m: In all the manvantaras, those are indeed the abodes of the gods. / Presiding deities occupy that abode again and again.

1.61.s:
atītaistu sahaitāni bhāvyābhāvyaiḥ suraiḥ saha
vartante vartamānaiś ca sthānibhistaiḥ suraiḥ saha //
1.61.d:
अतीतैस्तु सहैतानि भाव्याभाव्यैः सुरैः सह
वर्तन्ते वर्तमानैश् च स्थानिभिस्तैः सुरैः सह ॥
1.61.m: Together with past gods, with those yet to come and those who will not, / and together with present ones, [these abodes] endure along with those occupying gods.

1.61.s:
asminmanvantare caiva grahā vaimānikāḥ smṛtāḥ
vivasvānaditeḥ putraḥ sūryo vaivasvate 'ntare //
1.61.d:
अस्मिन्मन्वन्तरे चैव ग्रहा वैमानिकाः स्मृताः
विवस्वानदितेः पुत्रः सूर्यो वैवस्वते ऽन्तरे ॥
1.61.m: And in this manvantara, the planets are remembered as celestial-car riders. / In the Vaivasvata interval, the Sun is Vivasvat, son of Aditi.

1.61.s:
dyutimānṛṣiputrastu somo devo vasuḥ smṛtaḥ
śukro devastu vijñeyo bhārgavo 'surayājakaḥ //
1.61.d:
द्युतिमानृषिपुत्रस्तु सोमो देवो वसुः स्मृतः
शुक्रो देवस्तु विज्ञेयो भार्गवो ऽसुरयाजकः ॥
1.61.m: The luminous Soma, son of a sage, is known as a god and a Vasu; / Śukra, son of Bhṛgu, is to be known as a god and the priest of the asuras.

1.61.s:
bṛhattejāḥ smṛto devo devācāryo 'ṅgiraḥsutaḥ
budho manoharaścaiva ṛṣiputrastu sa smṛtaḥ //
1.61.d:
बृहत्तेजाः स्मृतो देवो देवाचार्यो ऽङ्गिरःसुतः
बुधो मनोहरश्चैव ऋषिपुत्रस्तु स स्मृतः ॥
1.61.m: The son of Aṅgiras of immense splendor is known as a god and the teacher of the gods; / Budha, attractive in appearance, is known as the son of a sage.

1.61.s:
śanaiścaro virūpastu saṃjñāputro vivasvataḥ
agnirvikeśyāṃ jajñe tu yuvāsau lohitārciṣaḥ //
1.61.d:
शनैश्चरो विरूपस्तु संज्ञापुत्रो विवस्वतः
अग्निर्विकेश्यां जज्ञे तु युवासौ लोहितार्चिषः ॥
1.61.m: Śanaiścara, deformity-bodied, was the son of Vivasvat through Saṃjñā; / while he, born of Vikeśī, is the youthful fire of red rays.

1.61.s:
nakṣatraṛkṣanāminyo dākṣāyaṇyastu tāḥ smṛtāḥ
svarbhānuḥ siṃhikāputro bhūtasaṃtāpano 'suraḥ //
1.61.d:
नक्षत्रऋक्षनामिन्यो दाक्षायण्यस्तु ताः स्मृताः
स्वर्भानुः सिंहिकापुत्रो भूतसंतापनो ऽसुरः ॥
1.61.m: The asterisms named nakṣatra and ṛkṣa are remembered as the daughters of Dakṣa; / Svarbhānu, son of Siṃhikā, is the asura who torments beings.

1.61.s:
somarkṣagrahasūryeṣu kīrtitāstvabhimāninaḥ
sthānānyetānyathoktāni sthāninyaścaiva devatāḥ //
1.61.d:
सोमर्क्षग्रहसूर्येषु कीर्तितास्त्वभिमानिनः
स्थानान्येतान्यथोक्तानि स्थानिन्यश्चैव देवताः ॥
1.61.m: These have been proclaimed as the presiding deities in the moon, the stars, the planets, and the sun; / and these abodes, as described, have these presiding deities.

1.61.s:
sauram agnimayaṃ sthānaṃ sahasrāṃśorvivasvataḥ
himāṃśostu smṛtaṃ sthānam ammayaṃ śuklameva ca //
1.61.d:
सौरम् अग्निमयं स्थानं सहस्रांशोर्विवस्वतः
हिमांशोस्तु स्मृतं स्थानम् अम्मयं शुक्लमेव च ॥
1.61.m: The abode of the thousand-rayed Vivasvat belongs to the sun and is full of fire; / that of the cool-rayed [moon] is remembered as made of water and white indeed.

1.61.s:
āpyaṃ śyāmaṃ manojñaṃ ca budharaśmigṛhaṃ smṛtam
śuklasyāpyammayaṃ śuklaṃ padaṃ ṣoḍaśaraśmivat //
1.61.d:
आप्यं श्यामं मनोज्ञं च बुधरश्मिगृहं स्मृतम्
शुक्लस्याप्यम्मयं शुक्लं पदं षोडशरश्मिवत् ॥
1.61.m: The abode of Budha's rays is remembered as watery, dark-hued, and pleasing; / the abode of Śukra is also watery, white, and possessed of sixteen rays.

1.61.s:
navaraśmi tu bhaumasya lohitaṃ sthānam uttamam
haridrābhaṃ bṛhaccāpi ṣoḍaśārcirbṛhaspateḥ //
1.61.d:
नवरश्मि तु भौमस्य लोहितं स्थानम् उत्तमम्
हरिद्राभं बृहच्चापि षोडशार्चिर्बृहस्पतेः ॥
1.61.m: The excellent abode of Bhauma has nine rays and is red; / and that of Bṛhaspati is turmeric-hued, vast, and possessed of sixteen rays.

1.61.s:
aṣṭaraśmigṛhaṃ cāpi proktaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ śanaiścare
svarbhānostāmasaṃ sthānaṃ bhūtasaṃtāpanālayam //
1.61.d:
अष्टरश्मिगृहं चापि प्रोक्तं कृष्णं शनैश्चरे
स्वर्भानोस्तामसं स्थानं भूतसंतापनालयम् ॥
1.61.m: The dark abode of Śanaiścara is declared to possess eight rays; / the dark abode of Svarbhānu is the tormenting habitation of living beings.

1.61.s:
vijñeyāstārakāḥ sarvās tv ṛṣayastvekaraśmayaḥ
āśrayāḥ puṇyakīrtīnāṃ śuklāścāpi svavarṇataḥ //
1.61.d:
विज्ञेयास्तारकाः सर्वास् त्व् ऋषयस्त्वेकरश्मयः
आश्रयाः पुण्यकीर्तीनां शुक्लाश्चापि स्ववर्णतः ॥
1.61.m: All the stars are to be known as having one ray, as are the sages; / they are the resorts of those of virtuous fame and are white by their natural color.

1.61.s:
ghanatoyātmikā jñeyāḥ kalpādāveva nirmitāḥ
ādityaraśmisaṃyogāt saṃprakāśātmikāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.61.d:
घनतोयात्मिका ज्ञेयाः कल्पादावेव निर्मिताः
आदित्यरश्मिसंयोगात् संप्रकाशात्मिकाः स्मृताः ॥
1.61.m: They are to be known as dense water in nature, fashioned right at the beginning of the kalpa; / they are remembered as luminous through their conjunction with the sun's rays.

1.61.s:
navayojanasāhasro viṣkaṃbhaḥ savituḥ smṛtaḥ
triguṇastasya vistāro maṇḍalasya pramāṇataḥ //
1.61.d:
नवयोजनसाहस्रो विष्कंभः सवितुः स्मृतः
त्रिगुणस्तस्य विस्तारो मण्डलस्य प्रमाणतः ॥
1.61.m: The diameter of the sun is remembered as nine thousand yojanas; / the circumference of that disc is three times that in measure.

1.61.s:
dviguṇaḥ sūryavistārād vistāraḥ śaśinaḥ smṛtaḥ
tulyastayostu svarbhānur bhūtvādhastātprasarpati //
1.61.d:
द्विगुणः सूर्यविस्ताराद् विस्तारः शशिनः स्मृतः
तुल्यस्तयोस्तु स्वर्भानुर् भूत्वाधस्तात्प्रसर्पति ॥
1.61.m: The diameter of the moon is remembered as twice the diameter of the sun; / equal to both of them, Svarbhānu creeps beneath them.

1.61.s:
uddhṛtya pṛthivīchāyāṃ nirmitāṃ maṇḍalākṛtim
svarbhānostu bṛhatsthānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ yattamomayam //
1.61.d:
उद्धृत्य पृथिवीछायां निर्मितां मण्डलाकृतिम्
स्वर्भानोस्तु बृहत्स्थानं तृतीयं यत्तमोमयम् ॥
1.61.m: Taking up the shadow of the earth, fashioned into the shape of a disc, / the great third abode of Svarbhānu is full of darkness.

1.61.s:
ādityāttacca niṣkramya samaṃ gacchati parvasu
ādityameti somācca punaḥ saureṣu parvasu //
1.61.d:
आदित्यात्तच्च निष्क्रम्य समं गच्छति पर्वसु
आदित्यमेति सोमाच्च पुनः सौरेषु पर्वसु ॥
1.61.m: Coming forth from the sun, it moves evenly at the joints [of the lunar phases]; / and from the moon it goes to the sun again during the solar joints.

1.61.s:
svarbhānuṃ nudate yasmāt tasmātsvarbhānurucyate
candrasya ṣoḍaśo bhāgo bhārgavasya vidhīyate //
1.61.d:
स्वर्भानुं नुदते यस्मात् तस्मात्स्वर्भानुरुच्यते
चन्द्रस्य षोडशो भागो भार्गवस्य विधीयते ॥
1.61.m: Because it dispels the sun's light, it is called Svarbhānu. / One sixteenth part of the moon is allotted to Śukra,

1.61.s:
viṣkaṃbhānmaṇḍalāccaiva yojanāgrātpramāṇataḥ
bhārgavātpādahīnastu vijñeyo vai bṛhaspatiḥ //
1.61.d:
विष्कंभान्मण्डलाच्चैव योजनाग्रात्प्रमाणतः
भार्गवात्पादहीनस्तु विज्ञेयो वै बृहस्पतिः ॥
1.61.m: in diameter and circumference, and in the total measure in yojanas. / Bṛhaspati is to be known as one fourth less than Śukra.

1.61.s:
bṛhaspateḥ pādahīnau vakrasaurī ubhau smṛtau
vistārānmaṇḍalāccaiva pādahīnastayorbudhaḥ //
1.61.d:
बृहस्पतेः पादहीनौ वक्रसौरी उभौ स्मृतौ
विस्तारान्मण्डलाच्चैव पादहीनस्तयोर्बुधः ॥
1.61.m: Both Vakra and Śauri are remembered as one fourth less than Bṛhaspati; / and Budha is one fourth less than the two in diameter and circumference.

1.61.s:
tārānakṣatrarūpāṇi vapuṣmantīha yāni vai
budhena tāni tulyāni vistārānmaṇḍalācca vai //
1.61.d:
तारानक्षत्ररूपाणि वपुष्मन्तीह यानि वै
बुधेन तानि तुल्यानि विस्तारान्मण्डलाच्च वै ॥
1.61.m: The embodied forms of the lunar mansions and stars here / are equal to Budha in diameter and circumference.

1.61.s:
prāyaśaścandrayogīni vidyādṛkṣāṇi tattvavit
tārānakṣatrarūpāṇi hīnāni tu parasparam //
1.61.d:
प्रायशश्चन्द्रयोगीनि विद्यादृक्षाणि तत्त्ववित्
तारानक्षत्ररूपाणि हीनानि तु परस्परम् ॥
1.61.m: The knower of truth should know that the asterisms are mostly conjoined with the moon; / the forms of the stars and lunar mansions are smaller than one another.

1.61.s:
śatāni pañca catvāri trīṇi dve caiva yojane
sarvopari nikṛṣṭāni tārakāmaṇḍalāni tu //
1.61.d:
शतानि पञ्च चत्वारि त्रीणि द्वे चैव योजने
सर्वोपरि निकृष्टानि तारकामण्डलानि तु ॥
1.61.m: The lowest discs of stars situated above all / are five, four, three, and two yojanas [in size];

1.61.s:
yojanānyardhamātrāṇi tebhyo hrasvaṃ na vidyate
upariṣṭāttrayasteṣāṃ grahāste dūrasarpiṇaḥ //
1.61.d:
योजनान्यर्धमात्राणि तेभ्यो ह्रस्वं न विद्यते
उपरिष्टात्त्रयस्तेषां ग्रहास्ते दूरसर्पिणः ॥
1.61.m: down to half a yojana; smaller than these there is none. / Above them are three planets that travel far.

1.61.s:
sauro 'ṅgirāś ca vakraś ca jñeyā mandavicāriṇaḥ
pūrvameva samākhyātā gatisteṣāṃ yathākramam //
1.61.d:
सौरो ऽङ्गिराश् च वक्रश् च ज्ञेया मन्दविचारिणः
पूर्वमेव समाख्याता गतिस्तेषां यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.61.m: Śauri, Āṅgirasa, and Vakra are to be known as slow-moving; / the movement of these in proper order has already been declared before.

1.61.s:
eteṣveva grahāḥ sarve nakṣatreṣu samutthitāḥ
vivasvānaditeḥ putraḥ sūryo vai munisattamāḥ //
1.61.d:
एतेष्वेव ग्रहाः सर्वे नक्षत्रेषु समुत्थिताः
विवस्वानदितेः पुत्रः सूर्यो वै मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
1.61.m: All the planets arose in these very nakṣatras: / the sun, Vivasvat, son of Aditi, O best of sages,

1.61.s:
viśākhāsu samutpanno grahāṇāṃ prathamo grahaḥ
tviṣimān dharmaputrastu somo devo vasustu saḥ //
1.61.d:
विशाखासु समुत्पन्नो ग्रहाणां प्रथमो ग्रहः
त्विषिमान् धर्मपुत्रस्तु सोमो देवो वसुस्तु सः ॥
1.61.m: the first planet among the planets, was born in Viśākhā; / the luminous god Soma, the Vasu, son of Dharma,

1.61.s:
śītaraśmiḥ samutpannaḥ kṛttikāsu niśākaraḥ
ṣoḍaśārcirbhṛgoḥ putraḥ śukraḥ sūryādanantaram //
1.61.d:
शीतरश्मिः समुत्पन्नः कृत्तिकासु निशाकरः
षोडशार्चिर्भृगोः पुत्रः शुक्रः सूर्यादनन्तरम् ॥
1.61.m: the cool-rayed night-maker, was born in Kṛttikā; / Śukra, the sixteen-rayed son of Bhṛgu, [born] right after the sun,

1.61.s:
tārāgrahāṇāṃ pravaras tiṣye kṣetre samutthitaḥ
grahaścāṅgirasaḥ putro dvādaśārcirbṛhaspatiḥ //
1.61.d:
ताराग्रहाणां प्रवरस् तिष्ये क्षेत्रे समुत्थितः
ग्रहश्चाङ्गिरसः पुत्रो द्वादशार्चिर्बृहस्पतिः ॥
1.61.m: foremost among the planet-stars, arose in the asterism Tiṣya; / the planet Bṛhaspati, the twelve-rayed son of Aṅgiras,

1.61.s:
phālgunīṣu samutpannaḥ pūrvākhyāsu jagadguruḥ
navārcirlohitāṅgaś ca prajāpatisuto grahaḥ //
1.61.d:
फाल्गुनीषु समुत्पन्नः पूर्वाख्यासु जगद्गुरुः
नवार्चिर्लोहिताङ्गश् च प्रजापतिसुतो ग्रहः ॥
1.61.m: the teacher of the universe, was born in the constellation called Pūrvaphālgunī; / the red-bodied planet of nine rays, son of Prajāpati,

1.61.s:
āṣāḍhāsviha pūrvāsu samutpanna iti smṛtaḥ
revatīṣveva saptārciḥsthāne sauriḥ śanaiścaraḥ //
1.61.d:
आषाढास्विह पूर्वासु समुत्पन्न इति स्मृतः
रेवतीष्वेव सप्तार्चिःस्थाने सौरिः शनैश्चरः ॥
1.61.m: is remembered as born here in Pūrvāṣāḍhā; / Śanaiścara, the son of the sun, seven-rayed, [arose] in the place of Revatī;

1.61.s:
saumyo budho dhaniṣṭhāsu pañcārcir udito grahaḥ
tamomayo mṛtyusutaḥ prajākṣayakaraḥ śikhī //
1.61.d:
सौम्यो बुधो धनिष्ठासु पञ्चार्चिर् उदितो ग्रहः
तमोमयो मृत्युसुतः प्रजाक्षयकरः शिखी ॥
1.61.m: Budha, the son of Soma, the five-rayed planet, arose in Dhaniṣṭhā; / Śikhin, full of darkness, son of Mṛtyu, causing the destruction of creatures,

1.61.s:
āśleṣāsu samutpannaḥ sarvahārī mahāgrahaḥ
tathā svanāmadheyeṣu dākṣāyaṇyaḥ samutthitāḥ //
1.61.d:
आश्लेषासु समुत्पन्नः सर्वहारी महाग्रहः
तथा स्वनामधेयेषु दाक्षायण्यः समुत्थिताः ॥
1.61.m: the great planet that snatches away all, was born in Āśleṣā; / likewise the daughters of Dakṣa arose in the asterisms named after themselves.

1.61.s:
tamovīryamayo rāhuḥ prakṛtyā kṛṣṇamaṇḍalaḥ
bharaṇīṣu samutpanno grahaścandrārkamardanaḥ //
1.61.d:
तमोवीर्यमयो राहुः प्रकृत्या कृष्णमण्डलः
भरणीषु समुत्पन्नो ग्रहश्चन्द्रार्कमर्दनः ॥
1.61.m: Rāhu, full of darkness and power, possessing a black disc by nature, / the planet that crushes the moon and the sun, was born in Bharaṇī.

1.61.s:
ete tārā grahāścāpi boddhavyā bhārgavādayaḥ
janmanakṣatrapīḍāsu yānti vaiguṇyatāṃ yataḥ //
1.61.d:
एते तारा ग्रहाश्चापि बोद्धव्या भार्गवादयः
जन्मनक्षत्रपीडासु यान्ति वैगुण्यतां यतः ॥
1.61.m: These stars and planets beginning with Śukra should also be understood: / since they become adverse during afflictions to one's birth star,

1.61.s:
mucyate tena doṣeṇa tatastadgrahabhaktitaḥ
sarvagrahāṇāmeteṣām ādirāditya ucyate //
1.61.d:
मुच्यते तेन दोषेण ततस्तद्ग्रहभक्तितः
सर्वग्रहाणामेतेषाम् आदिरादित्य उच्यते ॥
1.61.m: one is freed from that affliction through devotion to that planet. / The sun is declared to be the foremost among all these planets,

1.61.s:
tārāgrahāṇāṃ śukrastu ketūnāṃ cāpi dhūmavān
dhruvaḥ kila grahāṇāṃ tu vibhaktānāṃ caturdiśam //
1.61.d:
ताराग्रहाणां शुक्रस्तु केतूनां चापि धूमवान्
ध्रुवः किल ग्रहाणां तु विभक्तानां चतुर्दिशम् ॥
1.61.m: Śukra among the planet-stars, and Dhūmavān among the comets; / Dhruva is indeed [the foremost] among the planets distributed in the four quarters.

1.61.s:
nakṣatrāṇāṃ śraviṣṭhā syād ayanānāṃ tathottaram
varṣāṇāṃ caiva pañcānām ādyaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.61.d:
नक्षत्राणां श्रविष्ठा स्याद् अयनानां तथोत्तरम्
वर्षाणां चैव पञ्चानाम् आद्यः संवत्सरः स्मृतः ॥
1.61.m: Śraviṣṭhā is the first of the nakṣatras, and the northern is the first of the solstices; / of the five-year cycle, Saṃvatsara is remembered as the first;

1.61.s:
ṛtūnāṃ śiśiraścāpi māsānāṃ māgha ucyate
pakṣāṇāṃ śuklapakṣastu tithīnāṃ pratipattathā //
1.61.d:
ऋतूनां शिशिरश्चापि मासानां माघ उच्यते
पक्षाणां शुक्लपक्षस्तु तिथीनां प्रतिपत्तथा ॥
1.61.m: of the seasons, Śiśira; of the months, Māgha is declared [first]; / of the fortnights, the bright fortnight; and likewise Pratipad of the lunar days;

1.61.s:
ahorātravibhāgānām ahaścādiḥ prakīrtitaḥ
muhūrtānāṃ tathaivādir muhūrto rudradaivataḥ //
1.61.d:
अहोरात्रविभागानाम् अहश्चादिः प्रकीर्तितः
मुहूर्तानां तथैवादिर् मुहूर्तो रुद्रदैवतः ॥
1.61.m: of the divisions of day and night, the day is proclaimed as the first; / and likewise the first of the muhūrtas is the muhūrta that has Rudra as its deity;

1.61.s:
kṣaṇaścāpi nimeṣādiḥ kālaḥ kālavidāṃ varāḥ
śravaṇāntaṃ dhaniṣṭhādi yugaṃ syātpañcavārṣikam //
1.61.d:
क्षणश्चापि निमेषादिः कालः कालविदां वराः
श्रवणान्तं धनिष्ठादि युगं स्यात्पञ्चवार्षिकम् ॥
1.61.m: and the kṣaṇa is the beginning of the nimeṣa and others, O best of the knowers of time. / The five-year yuga begins with Dhaniṣṭhā and ends with Śravaṇa.

1.61.s:
bhānorgativiśeṣeṇa cakravatparivartate
divākaraḥ smṛtastasmāt kālakṛdvibhurīśvaraḥ //
1.61.d:
भानोर्गतिविशेषेण चक्रवत्परिवर्तते
दिवाकरः स्मृतस्तस्मात् कालकृद्विभुरीश्वरः ॥
1.61.m: Through the distinct motion of the sun, it turns like a wheel; / therefore the sun is remembered as the maker of time, the all-pervading lord,

1.61.s:
caturvidhānāṃ bhūtānāṃ pravartakanivartakaḥ
tasyāpi bhagavān rudraḥ sākṣāddevaḥ pravartakaḥ //
1.61.d:
चतुर्विधानां भूतानां प्रवर्तकनिवर्तकः
तस्यापि भगवान् रुद्रः साक्षाद्देवः प्रवर्तकः ॥
1.61.m: the instigator and withdrawer of the four kinds of living beings; / and of him too, the lord Rudra himself, the visible god, is the instigator.

1.61.s:
ityeṣa jyotiṣāmevaṃ saṃniveśo 'rthaniścayaḥ
lokasaṃvyavahārārthaṃ mahādevena nirmitaḥ //
1.61.d:
इत्येष ज्योतिषामेवं संनिवेशो ऽर्थनिश्चयः
लोकसंव्यवहारार्थं महादेवेन निर्मितः ॥
1.61.m: Thus this arrangement of the heavenly bodies and determination of their meaning / was created by Mahādeva for the sake of worldly transactions.

1.61.s:
buddhipūrvaṃ bhagavatā kalpādau sampravartitaḥ
sa āśrayo 'bhimānī ca sarvasya jyotirātmakaḥ //
1.61.d:
बुद्धिपूर्वं भगवता कल्पादौ सम्प्रवर्तितः
स आश्रयो ऽभिमानी च सर्वस्य ज्योतिरात्मकः ॥
1.61.m: Deliberately set into motion by the Lord at the beginning of the kalpa, / he is the support and presiding deity of everything, consisting of light.

1.61.s:
ekarūpapradhānasya pariṇāmo 'yamadbhutaḥ
naiṣa śakyaḥ prasaṃkhyātuṃ yāthātathyena kenacit //
1.61.d:
एकरूपप्रधानस्य परिणामो ऽयमद्भुतः
नैष शक्यः प्रसंख्यातुं याथातथ्येन केनचित् ॥
1.61.m: This is a wonderful transformation of Pradhāna, which has a single nature; / it is not possible for anyone to calculate it in its true reality.

1.61.s:
gatāgataṃ manuṣyeṇa jyotiṣāṃ māṃsacakṣuṣā
āgamādanumānācca pratyakṣādupapattitaḥ //
1.61.d:
गतागतं मनुष्येण ज्योतिषां मांसचक्षुषा
आगमादनुमानाच्च प्रत्यक्षादुपपत्तितः ॥
1.61.m: The coming and going of the heavenly bodies [cannot be fully known] by a human being with the physical eye; / through tradition, inference, perception, and logical reason,

1.61.s:
parīkṣya nipuṇaṃ buddhyā śraddhātavyaṃ vipaścitā
cakṣuḥ śāstraṃ jalaṃ lekhyaṃ gaṇitaṃ munisattamāḥ //
1.61.d:
परीक्ष्य निपुणं बुद्ध्या श्रद्धातव्यं विपश्चिता
चक्षुः शास्त्रं जलं लेख्यं गणितं मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
1.61.m: having examined it thoroughly with intellect, the wise person should place faith in it. / The eye, sacred scripture, water, writing, and calculation, O best of sages—

1.61.s: pañcaite hetavo jñeyā jyotirmānavinirṇaye //
1.61.d: पञ्चैते हेतवो ज्ञेया ज्योतिर्मानविनिर्णये ॥
1.61.m: these five are to be known as the means for determining the measure of the luminaries.

1.62.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
kathaṃ viṣṇoḥ prasādādvai dhruvo buddhimatāṃ varaḥ
meḍhībhūto grāhāṇāṃ vai vaktumarhasi sāṃpratam //
1.62.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
कथं विष्णोः प्रसादाद्वै ध्रुवो बुद्धिमतां वरः
मेढीभूतो ग्राहाणां वै वक्तुमर्हसि सांप्रतम् ॥
1.62.m: The sages said: / How, by the grace of Viṣṇu, did Dhruva, the best of the wise, / become the pivot of the planets? You should tell us now.

1.62.s:
sūta uvāca
etamarthaṃ mayā pṛṣṭo nānāśāstraviśāradaḥ
mārkaṇḍeyaḥ purā prāha mahyaṃ śuśrūṣave dvijāḥ //
1.62.d:
सूत उवाच
एतमर्थं मया पृष्टो नानाशास्त्रविशारदः
मार्कण्डेयः पुरा प्राह मह्यं शुश्रूषवे द्विजाः ॥
1.62.m:
Sūta said:
When questioned by me on this matter in the past, Mārkaṇḍeya, versed in various treatises, / spoke [thus] to me as I wished to hear, O twice-born.

Mārkaṇḍeya said:
King Uttānapāda, indeed an emperor of great majesty, / the best among all wielders of weapons, protected the earth.

He had two wives: Sunīti and Suruci. / A son of great fame was born to the elder wife, Sunīti:

named Dhruva, highly wise, the lamp of his lineage, of great intellect. / Once, although only seven years old, he climbed onto his father's lap.

Repulsing him, Suruci, with delight in her heart / and proud of her beauty, O best of sages, placed her own son on his lap.

Not gaining his father's lap, the wise [boy], his mind aggrieved, / approached his mother and wept again and again.

His mother, overcome with grief, said this to her weeping son: / 'Suruci is the beloved of her husband, and her son is like her.

You are born to me, an unfortunate woman, and so you too are unfortunate. / Why do you lament? For what purpose do you weep again and again?

Becoming afflicted at heart, you will cause me grief. / By your own power, O son, you should attain a firm, secure place.'

Having been spoken to thus by his mother, he went forth to the forest at that time. / Seeing Viśvāmitra there, he bowed down according to the rules,

and with folded hands said: 'O venerable one, you should speak; / by what means shall I attain a place above all others, O best of the virtuous?

O sage, as I was sitting on my father's lap, my mother Suruci / brushed me away; the king, my father, said nothing at all to him.

For that reason, O Brahman, terrified I went to my mother. / My mother Sunīti said to me: "Do not grieve so exceedingly;

by your own deeds you ought to attain the highest place, my dear son." / Hearing her words, O great sage, I sought your abode,

and have reached this forest, O Brahman; today I have seen you, O lord. / By your grace I shall attain a wondrous, highest place.'

Addressed thus, that glorious sage laughed and said this: / 'O prince, listen to this; you will attain the highest place

by worshipping the lord of the worlds, Keśava, the destroyer of affliction, / who sprang from the right side of Śambhu, the wise Mahādeva.

Constantly chant, O greatly wise one, that which destroys all sins, / grants desires, is supreme, pure, holy, spotless, and transcendent.

Utter this divine mantra endowed with the Praṇava: / "Salutation be to Vāsudeva!" With restrained senses,

meditating on the eternal Viṣṇu, devoted to chanting and oblations.' / Spoken to thus, the highly renowned [prince] bowed to Viśvāmitra,

and facing east, self-restrained, chanted with a joyful heart, / subsisting on greens, roots, and fruits, unwearied for a year.

Ceaselessly and perpetually he chanted the mantra again and again. / Dreadful vetālas, rākṣasas, lions, and other great wild beasts,

terrific ones, approached that great-souled one to bewilder his mind; / chanting 'Vāsudeva', he did not notice anything at all.

Assuming the form of Sunīti, his mother, / a piśācī arrived and wept, exceedingly sorrowful:

'You are my only son; why do you torment yourself? / Abandoning me who am helpless, you have undertaken austerity!'

While she was uttering these and other words, the great ascetic, / joyful in heart, chanted the name of Hari without even looking at her.

Then all forms of obstacles subsided everywhere there. / Thereupon, mounting Garuḍa, radiant like a dark raincloud,

surrounded by all the gods and praised by great sages, / the Lord Viṣṇu, the slayer of foes, arrived near Dhruva.

Seeing that he had arrived, Dhruva wondered, 'Who is he?' / and as though drinking in Hṛṣīkeśa, the lord of the world, with his eyes,

stood chanting 'Vāsudeva', endowed with great radiance. / Then Govinda touched his mouth with the edge of his conch.

Thereupon, having obtained supreme knowledge, / with folded hands he praised Hari, the Supreme Puruṣa, the lord of all worlds:

'Be gracious, O Lord of the gods of gods, bearer of the conch, discus, and mace! / O Self of the worlds, whose essence is the secret of the Vedas, I have taken refuge in you, O Keśava!

The great sages beginning with Sanaka do not know you, the Great-souled one; / so how could I know you? Salutations to you, O Lord of the universe!'

Smiling, Viṣṇu said to him: 'Come, my child, you shall be Dhruva (firm); / having attained a fixed abode, become the first consumer [of oblations] among the celestial luminaries.

Together with your mother, attain there the abode of the celestial luminaries. / This supreme abode of mine is Dhruva (fixed), eternal, and very auspicious.

It was obtained in the past from Śaṅkara by worshipping the Lord of gods through austerity. / The wise man who constantly chants "to Vāsudeva", / accompanied by the Praṇava, united with salutation, and joined with the word "Bhagavat" (i.e. "Oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya"), / indeed attains the fixed (dhruva) abode.'

Then the gods along with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the supreme sages, / established Dhruva together with his mother in that abode.

Honouring the command of Viṣṇu, he attained the abode of the celestial luminaries. / Thus Dhruva, of great majesty, by means of the twelve-syllable mantra,

attained great perfection. This has been related to you by me.

Sūta said:
Therefore, the man who offers salutation to Vāsudeva / goes to the same realm as Dhruva, and likewise his firm stability [is assured].

Thus ends the sixty-second chapter, entitled 'Description of the Abode of Dhruva', in the Bhuvana-kośa section of the first part of the venerable Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa.

The sages said:
O Sūta, speak today in proper and unsurpassed order / of the origin of the gods, dānavas, gandharvas, serpents, and rakṣasas.

Sūta said:
The creation of the ancients is said to have occurred through intention, sight, and touch; / after Dakṣa, son of Pracetas, creation arose from sexual union.

When, as he was creating, the hosts of gods, sages, and serpents / did not increase the world, then through the practice of sexual union,

Dakṣa begat five thousand sons upon the mother (his wife Asiknī). / Seeing those fortunate ones, Nārada, wishing to have diverse creatures created,

said to the Haryaśvas, the sons of Dakṣa who had gathered: / 'Having known the entire extent of the earth, above as well as below,

then, O best of sages, carry out creation especially!' / Hearing his words, they departed in all directions.

1.62.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
sārvabhaumo mahātejāḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
uttānapādo rājā vai pālayāmāsa medinīm //
1.62.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
सार्वभौमो महातेजाः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः
उत्तानपादो राजा वै पालयामास मेदिनीम् ॥
1.62.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / King Uttānapāda, indeed a universal monarch of great splendor / and the best of all wielders of weapons, protected the earth.

1.62.s:
tasya bhāryādvayam abhūt sunītiḥ surucis tathā
agrajāyāmabhūtputraḥ sunītyāṃ tu mahāyaśāḥ //
1.62.d:
तस्य भार्याद्वयम् अभूत् सुनीतिः सुरुचिस् तथा
अग्रजायामभूत्पुत्रः सुनीत्यां तु महायशाः ॥
1.62.m: He had two wives: Sunīti and Suruci. / To his elder wife, Sunīti, was born a highly renowned son,

1.62.s:
dhruvo nāma mahāprājñaḥ kuladīpo mahāmatiḥ
kadācit saptavarṣe 'pi pituraṅkam upāviśat //
1.62.d:
ध्रुवो नाम महाप्राज्ञः कुलदीपो महामतिः
कदाचित् सप्तवर्षे ऽपि पितुरङ्कम् उपाविशत् ॥
1.62.m: named Dhruva, of great wisdom, the lamp of his lineage, of noble intellect. / Once, although only seven years of age, he climbed into his father’s lap.

1.62.s:
surucistaṃ vinirdhūya svaputraṃ prītimānasā
nyaveśayattaṃ viprendrā hy aṅkaṃ rūpeṇa mānitā //
1.62.d:
सुरुचिस्तं विनिर्धूय स्वपुत्रं प्रीतिमानसा
न्यवेशयत्तं विप्रेन्द्रा ह्य् अङ्कं रूपेण मानिता ॥
1.62.m:
Suruci pushed him away, O foremost of Brahmins; having a delighted mind,
puffed up with pride in her beauty, she placed her own son upon the lap.

1.62.s:
alabdhvā sa piturdhīmān aṅkaṃ duḥkhitamānasaḥ
mātuḥ samīpamāgamya ruroda sa punaḥ punaḥ //
1.62.d:
अलब्ध्वा स पितुर्धीमान् अङ्कं दुःखितमानसः
मातुः समीपमागम्य रुरोद स पुनः पुनः ॥
1.62.m:
Not receiving his father's lap, the wise boy, distressed in mind,
came to his mother and wept again and again.

1.62.s:
rudantaṃ putramāhedaṃ mātā śokapariplutā
surucirdayitā bhartus tasyāḥ putro 'pi tādṛśaḥ //
1.62.d:
रुदन्तं पुत्रमाहेदं माता शोकपरिप्लुता
सुरुचिर्दयिता भर्तुस् तस्याः पुत्रो ऽपि तादृशः ॥
1.62.m:
To her weeping son, the mother, overwhelmed with grief, said this:
“Suruci is the beloved of her husband, and her son is like her.

1.62.s:
mama tvaṃ mandabhāgyāyā jātaḥ putro 'pyabhāgyavān
kiṃ śocasi kimarthaṃ tvaṃ rodamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ //
1.62.d:
मम त्वं मन्दभाग्याया जातः पुत्रो ऽप्यभाग्यवान्
किं शोचसि किमर्थं त्वं रोदमानः पुनः पुनः ॥
1.62.m:
You were born of me, an unfortunate woman, as a son who is also unfortunate.
Why do you grieve? Why are you weeping again and again?

1.62.s:
saṃtaptahṛdayo bhūtvā mama śokaṃ kariṣyasi
svasthasthānaṃ dhruvaṃ putra svaśaktyā tvaṃ samāpnuyāḥ //
1.62.d:
संतप्तहृदयो भूत्वा मम शोकं करिष्यसि
स्वस्थस्थानं ध्रुवं पुत्र स्वशक्त्या त्वं समाप्नुयाः ॥
1.62.m:
Becoming heart-stricken, you will cause me grief.
By your own power, O son, you should attain a firm, secure place.”

1.62.s:
ityuktaḥ sa tu mātrā vai nirjagāma tadā vanam
viśvāmitraṃ tato dṛṣṭvā praṇipatya yathāvidhi //
1.62.d:
इत्युक्तः स तु मात्रा वै निर्जगाम तदा वनम्
विश्वामित्रं ततो दृष्ट्वा प्रणिपत्य यथाविधि ॥
1.62.m:
Thus addressed by his mother, he then went out to the forest.
Thereupon, having seen Viśvāmitra and bowed down to him in accordance with rule,

1.62.s:
uvāca prāñjalirbhūtvā bhagavan vaktumarhasi
sarveṣāmuparisthānaṃ kena prāpsyāmi sattama //
1.62.d:
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा भगवन् वक्तुमर्हसि
सर्वेषामुपरिस्थानं केन प्राप्स्यामि सत्तम ॥
1.62.m:
with folded hands, he said: “O Lord, you ought to tell [me]:
by what means shall I attain a place above all [others], O best of beings?

1.62.s:
pituraṅke samāsīnaṃ mātā māṃ surucirmune
vyadhūnayatsa taṃ rājā pitā novāca kiṃcana //
1.62.d:
पितुरङ्के समासीनं माता मां सुरुचिर्मुने
व्यधूनयत्स तं राजा पिता नोवाच किंचन ॥
1.62.m:
As I was seated on my father's lap, O sage, my [step]mother Suruci
thrust me aside, and the king, my father, said nothing at all to her.

1.62.s:
etasmāt kāraṇād brahmaṃs trasto 'haṃ mātaraṃ gataḥ
sunītirāha me mātā mā kṛthāḥ śokamuttamam //
1.62.d:
एतस्मात् कारणाद् ब्रह्मंस् त्रस्तो ऽहं मातरं गतः
सुनीतिराह मे माता मा कृथाः शोकमुत्तमम् ॥
1.62.m:
For this reason, O Brahmin, I went frightened to my mother.
My mother Sunīti said to me: ‘Do not give way to great grief.

1.62.s:
svakarmaṇā paraṃ sthānaṃ prāptumarhasi putraka
tasyā hi vacanaṃ śrutvā sthānaṃ tava mahāmune //
1.62.d:
स्वकर्मणा परं स्थानं प्राप्तुमर्हसि पुत्रक
तस्या हि वचनं श्रुत्वा स्थानं तव महामुने ॥
1.62.m:
You ought to attain the highest place by your own deed, my child.’
Having heard her words, indeed, [seeking] your abode, O great sage,

1.62.s:
prāpto vanamidaṃ brahmann adya tvāṃ dṛṣṭavānprabho
tava prasādāt prāpsye 'haṃ sthānamadbhutamuttamam //
1.62.d:
प्राप्तो वनमिदं ब्रह्मन्न् अद्य त्वां दृष्टवान्प्रभो
तव प्रसादात् प्राप्स्ये ऽहं स्थानमद्भुतमुत्तमम् ॥
1.62.m:
I have reached this forest, O Brahmin. Today I have seen you, O lord.
By your grace I shall attain a wondrous, highest place.”

1.62.s:
ityuktaḥ sa muniḥ śrīmān prahasann idam abravīt
rājaputra śṛṇuṣvedaṃ sthānamuttamamāpsyasi //
1.62.d:
इत्युक्तः स मुनिः श्रीमान् प्रहसन्न् इदम् अब्रवीत्
राजपुत्र शृणुष्वेदं स्थानमुत्तममाप्स्यसि ॥
1.62.m:
Thus addressed, the illustrious sage smiled and said this:
“O prince, listen to this: you shall attain the highest place.

1.62.s:
ārādhya jagatāmīśaṃ keśavaṃ kleśanāśanam
dakṣiṇāṅgabhavaṃ śaṃbhor mahādevasya dhīmataḥ //
1.62.d:
आराध्य जगतामीशं केशवं क्लेशनाशनम्
दक्षिणाङ्गभवं शंभोर् महादेवस्य धीमतः ॥
1.62.m:
By worshipping Keśava, the lord of the worlds, the destroyer of affliction,
born from the right side of Śambhu, wise Mahādeva,

1.62.s:
japa nityaṃ mahāprājña sarvapāpavināśanam
iṣṭadaṃ paramaṃ śuddhaṃ pavitramamalaṃ param //
1.62.d:
जप नित्यं महाप्राज्ञ सर्वपापविनाशनम्
इष्टदं परमं शुद्धं पवित्रममलं परम् ॥
1.62.m:
constantly chant, O greatly wise one, the destroyer of all sins,
the granter of desires, the supreme, pure, sacred, immaculate, highest [mantra].

1.62.s:
brūhi mantramimaṃ divyaṃ praṇavena samanvitam
namo 'stu vāsudevāya ityevaṃ niyatendriyaḥ //
1.62.d:
ब्रूहि मन्त्रमिमं दिव्यं प्रणवेन समन्वितम्
नमो ऽस्तु वासुदेवाय इत्येवं नियतेन्द्रियः ॥
1.62.m:
Utter this divine mantra equipped with the praṇava:
‘Reverence be to Vāsudeva,’ with senses restrained in this manner,

1.62.s:
dhyāyansanātanaṃ viṣṇuṃ japahomaparāyaṇaḥ
ityuktaḥ praṇipatyainaṃ viśvāmitraṃ mahāyaśāḥ //
1.62.d:
ध्यायन्सनातनं विष्णुं जपहोमपरायणः
इत्युक्तः प्रणिपत्यैनं विश्वामित्रं महायशाः ॥
1.62.m:
meditating upon the eternal Viṣṇu, devoted to chanting and oblations.”
Thus addressed, having bowed down to Viśvāmitra, the highly renowned [boy],

1.62.s:
prāṅmukho niyato bhūtvā jajāpa prītamānasaḥ
śākamūlaphalāhāraḥ saṃvatsaramatandritaḥ //
1.62.d:
प्राङ्मुखो नियतो भूत्वा जजाप प्रीतमानसः
शाकमूलफलाहारः संवत्सरमतन्द्रितः ॥
1.62.m:
facing east and self-restrained, chanted with a delighted mind,
subsisting on vegetables, roots, and fruits, unwearied for a year.

1.62.s:
jajāpa mantramaniśam ajasraṃ sa punaḥ punaḥ
vetālā rākṣasā ghorāḥ siṃhādyāś ca mahāmṛgāḥ //
1.62.d:
जजाप मन्त्रमनिशम् अजस्रं स पुनः पुनः
वेताला राक्षसा घोराः सिंहाद्याश् च महामृगाः ॥
1.62.m:
Day and night he chanted the mantra uninterruptedly, again and again.
Formidable vetālas, rākṣasas, lions, and other great wild beasts

1.62.s:
tamabhyayurmahātmānaṃ buddhimohāya bhīṣaṇāḥ
japan sa vāsudeveti na kiṃcit pratyapadyata //
1.62.d:
तमभ्ययुर्महात्मानं बुद्धिमोहाय भीषणाः
जपन् स वासुदेवेति न किंचित् प्रत्यपद्यत ॥
1.62.m:
approached that great-souled one, terrifying, in order to confuse his mind.
Chanting “Vāsudeva”, he noticed nothing [of them].

1.62.s:
sunītir asya yā mātā tasyā rūpeṇa saṃvṛtā
piśāci samanuprāptā ruroda bhṛśaduḥkhitā //
1.62.d:
सुनीतिर् अस्य या माता तस्या रूपेण संवृता
पिशाचि समनुप्राप्ता रुरोद भृशदुःखिता ॥
1.62.m:
Veiled in the form of Sunīti, who was his mother,
a piśācī arrived and wept, exceedingly distressed:

1.62.s:
mama tvamekaḥ putro 'si kimarthaṃ kliśyate bhavān
māmanāthāmapahāya tapa āsthitavānasi //
1.62.d:
मम त्वमेकः पुत्रो ऽसि किमर्थं क्लिश्यते भवान्
मामनाथामपहाय तप आस्थितवानसि ॥
1.62.m:
“You are my only son; why are you tormenting yourself?
Having abandoned me, a helpless woman, you have undertaken asceticism!”

1.62.s:
evamādīni vākyāni bhāṣamāṇāṃ mahātapāḥ
anirīkṣyaiva hṛṣṭātmā harernāma jajāpa saḥ //
1.62.d:
एवमादीनि वाक्यानि भाषमाणां महातपाः
अनिरीक्ष्यैव हृष्टात्मा हरेर्नाम जजाप सः ॥
1.62.m:
To her speaking words such as these, the one of great austerities,
without even looking at her, with gladdened soul, chanted the name of Hari.

1.62.s:
tataḥ praśemuḥ sarvatra vighnarūpāṇi tatra vai
tato garuḍamāruhya kālameghasamadyutiḥ //
1.62.d:
ततः प्रशेमुः सर्वत्र विघ्नरूपाणि तत्र वै
ततो गरुडमारुह्य कालमेघसमद्युतिः ॥
1.62.m:
Then, all around, the forms of obstacles were entirely pacified.
Thereupon, having mounted Garuḍa, with the brilliance of a dark cloud,

1.62.s:
sarvadevaiḥ parivṛtaḥ stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ
āyayau bhagavānviṣṇuḥ dhruvāntikam arātihā //
1.62.d:
सर्वदेवैः परिवृतः स्तूयमानो महर्षिभिः
आययौ भगवान्विष्णुः ध्रुवान्तिकम् अरातिहा ॥
1.62.m:
surrounded by all the gods, praised by the great sages,
Lord Viṣṇu, the slayer of foes, came near to Dhruva.

1.62.s:
samāgataṃ vilokyātha ko 'sāvityeva cintayan
pibanniva hṛṣīkeśaṃ nayanābhyāṃ jagatpatim //
1.62.d:
समागतं विलोक्याथ को ऽसावित्येव चिन्तयन्
पिबन्निव हृषीकेशं नयनाभ्यां जगत्पतिम् ॥
1.62.m:
Seeing him arrived, thinking, “Who is he?”,
as if drinking in Hṛṣīkeśa, the lord of the world, with his eyes,

1.62.s:
japan sa vāsudeveti dhruvastasthau mahādyutiḥ
śaṅkhaprāntena govindaḥ pasparśāsyaṃ hi tasya vai //
1.62.d:
जपन् स वासुदेवेति ध्रुवस्तस्थौ महाद्युतिः
शङ्खप्रान्तेन गोविन्दः पस्पर्शास्यं हि तस्य वै ॥
1.62.m:
chanting “Vāsudeva”, Dhruva of great splendour stood.
Then Govinda touched his face with the tip of his conch.

1.62.s:
tataḥ sa paramaṃ jñānam avāpya puruṣottamam
tuṣṭāva prāñjalirbhūtvā sarvalokeśvaraṃ harim //
1.62.d:
ततः स परमं ज्ञानम् अवाप्य पुरुषोत्तमम्
तुष्टाव प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा सर्वलोकेश्वरं हरिम् ॥
1.62.m:
Then, having attained supreme knowledge, he, with folded hands,
praised Hari, Puruṣottama, the lord of all the worlds:

1.62.s:
prasīda devadeveśa śaṅkhacakragadādhara
lokātman vedaguhyātman tvāṃ prapanno 'smi keśava //
1.62.d:
प्रसीद देवदेवेश शङ्खचक्रगदाधर
लोकात्मन् वेदगुह्यात्मन् त्वां प्रपन्नो ऽस्मि केशव ॥
1.62.m:
“Be gracious, O Lord of the gods of gods, bearer of conch, discus, and mace,
Soul of the world, Soul hidden in the Veda! I have taken refuge in you, O Keśava!

1.62.s:
na vidustvāṃ mahātmānaṃ sanakādyā maharṣayaḥ
tatkathaṃ tvāmahaṃ vidyāṃ namaste bhuvaneśvara //
1.62.d:
न विदुस्त्वां महात्मानं सनकाद्या महर्षयः
तत्कथं त्वामहं विद्यां नमस्ते भुवनेश्वर ॥
1.62.m:
The great sages, Sanaka and others, do not know your great soul;
then how could I know you? Reverence to you, O Lord of the universe!”

1.62.s:
tamāha prahasanviṣṇur ehi vatsa dhruvo bhavān
sthānaṃ dhruvaṃ samāsādya jyotiṣām agrabhug bhava //
1.62.d:
तमाह प्रहसन्विष्णुर् एहि वत्स ध्रुवो भवान्
स्थानं ध्रुवं समासाद्य ज्योतिषाम् अग्रभुग् भव ॥
1.62.m:
Smiling, Viṣṇu said to him: “Come, my child, you are Dhruva.
Having attained the firm (dhruva) station, become the foremost enjoyer of the luminaries.

1.62.s:
mātrā tvaṃ sahitastatra jyotiṣāṃ sthānamāpnuhi
matsthānametatparamaṃ dhruvaṃ nityaṃ suśobhanam //
1.62.d:
मात्रा त्वं सहितस्तत्र ज्योतिषां स्थानमाप्नुहि
मत्स्थानमेतत्परमं ध्रुवं नित्यं सुशोभनम् ॥
1.62.m:
Together with your mother, attain there the station of the luminaries.
This supreme, firm, eternal, and exceedingly splendid station of mine

1.62.s:
tapasārādhya deveśaṃ purā labdhaṃ hi śaṅkarāt
vāsudeveti yo nityaṃ praṇavena samanvitam //
1.62.d:
तपसाराध्य देवेशं पुरा लब्धं हि शङ्करात्
वासुदेवेति यो नित्यं प्रणवेन समन्वितम् ॥
1.62.m:
was obtained in the past from Śaṅkara by worshipping the Lord of the gods through asceticism.
Whichever wise man constantly chants

1.62.s:
namaskārasamāyuktaṃ bhagavacchabdasaṃyutam
japedevaṃ hi yo vidvān dhruvaṃ sthānaṃ prapadyate //
1.62.d:
नमस्कारसमायुक्तं भगवच्छब्दसंयुतम्
जपेदेवं हि यो विद्वान् ध्रुवं स्थानं प्रपद्यते ॥
1.62.m:
‘Vāsudeva’, joined with the praṇava,
accompanied by salutation and combined with the word ‘Bhagavat’,
indeed attains the firm (dhruva) station.”

1.62.s:
tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
mātrā saha dhruvaṃ sarve tasmin sthāne nyaveśayan //
1.62.d:
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश् च परमर्षयः
मात्रा सह ध्रुवं सर्वे तस्मिन् स्थाने न्यवेशयन् ॥
1.62.m:
Then the gods along with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the highest sages
placed Dhruva along with his mother in that station.

1.62.s:
viṣṇorājñāṃ puraskṛtya jyotiṣāṃ sthānamāptavān
evaṃ dhruvo mahātejā dvādaśākṣaravidyayā //
1.62.d:
विष्णोराज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य ज्योतिषां स्थानमाप्तवान्
एवं ध्रुवो महातेजा द्वादशाक्षरविद्यया ॥
1.62.m:
Putting Viṣṇu’s command foremost, he obtained the station of the luminaries.
Thus Dhruva of great splendour, by means of the twelve-syllable formula,

1.62.s: avāpa mahatīṃ siddhim etatte kathitaṃ mayā //
1.62.d: अवाप महतीं सिद्धिम् एतत्ते कथितं मया ॥
1.62.m: attained great perfection. This has been related to you by me.

1.62.s:
sūta uvāca
tasmādyo vāsudevāya praṇāmaṃ kurute naraḥ
sa yāti dhruvasālokyaṃ dhruvatvaṃ tasya tattathā //
1.62.d:
सूत उवाच
तस्माद्यो वासुदेवाय प्रणामं कुरुते नरः
स याति ध्रुवसालोक्यं ध्रुवत्वं तस्य तत्तथा ॥
1.62.m:
Sūta said:
Therefore, whatever man performs obeisance to Vāsudeva
goes to the realm of Dhruva, and firmness belongs to him in just that way.

1.63.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca gandharvoragarakṣasām
utpattiṃ brūhi sūtādya yathākramamanuttamam //
1.63.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
देवानां दानवानां च गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम्
उत्पत्तिं ब्रूहि सूताद्य यथाक्रममनुत्तमम् ॥
1.63.m:
The sages said:
Speak today, O Sūta, of the unsurpassed origin in due order
of the gods, dānavas, gandharvas, serpents, and rākṣasas.

1.63.s:
sūta uvāca
saṃkalpāddarśanātsparśāt pūrveṣāṃ sṛṣṭirucyate
dakṣātprācetasādūrdhvaṃ sṛṣṭirmaithunasaṃbhavā //
1.63.d:
सूत उवाच
संकल्पाद्दर्शनात्स्पर्शात् पूर्वेषां सृष्टिरुच्यते
दक्षात्प्राचेतसादूर्ध्वं सृष्टिर्मैथुनसंभवा ॥

1.63.s:
yadā tu sṛjatastasya devarṣigaṇapannagān
na vṛddhimagamallokas tadā maithunayogataḥ //
1.63.d:
यदा तु सृजतस्तस्य देवर्षिगणपन्नगान्
न वृद्धिमगमल्लोकस् तदा मैथुनयोगतः ॥
1.63.m:
When, as he created the hosts of divine sages and serpents,
the world did not increase, then, through the union of copulation,

1.63.s:
dakṣaḥ putrasahasrāṇi pañca sūtyāmajījanat
tāṃstu dṛṣṭvā mahābhāgān sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ //
1.63.d:
दक्षः पुत्रसहस्राणि पञ्च सूत्यामजीजनत्
तांस्तु दृष्ट्वा महाभागान् सिसृक्षुर्विविधाः प्रजाः ॥
1.63.m:
Dakṣa begot five thousand sons on Sūtī.
Seeing those highly fortunate ones, desirous of creating diverse offspring,

1.63.s:
nāradaḥ prāha haryaśvān dakṣaputrān samāgatān
bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ tu jñātvordhvamadha eva ca //
1.63.d:
नारदः प्राह हर्यश्वान् दक्षपुत्रान् समागतान्
भुवः प्रमाणं सर्वं तु ज्ञात्वोर्ध्वमध एव च ॥
1.63.m:
Nārada spoke to the Haryaśvas, the sons of Dakṣa who had assembled:
“Having known the entire extent of the earth, both above and below,

1.63.s:
tataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ viśeṣeṇa kurudhvaṃ munisattamāḥ
te tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā prayātāḥ sarvatodiśam //
1.63.d:
ततः सृष्टिं विशेषेण कुरुध्वं मुनिसत्तमाः
ते तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रयाताः सर्वतोदिशम् ॥
1.63.m:
then produce creation in particular, O best of sages!”
Having heard his words, they went off in every direction.

1.63.s:
adyāpi na nivartante samudrādiva sindhavaḥ
haryaśveṣu ca naṣṭeṣu punardakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ //
1.63.d:
अद्यापि न निवर्तन्ते समुद्रादिव सिन्धवः
हर्यश्वेषु च नष्टेषु पुनर्दक्षः प्रजापतिः ॥
1.63.m:
Even today they do not return, just as rivers do not return from the ocean.
And when the Haryaśvas were lost, the lord Prajāpati Dakṣa

1.63.s:
sūtyāmeva ca putrāṇāṃ sahasramasṛjatprabhuḥ
śabalā nāma te viprāḥ sametāḥ sṛṣṭihetavaḥ //
1.63.d:
सूत्यामेव च पुत्राणां सहस्रमसृजत्प्रभुः
शबला नाम ते विप्राः समेताः सृष्टिहेतवः ॥
1.63.m:
again created on Sūtī a thousand sons.
They were named Śabalas, O Brahmins, gathered for the purpose of creation.

1.63.s:
nārado 'nugatānprāha punastānsūryavarcasaḥ
bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ tu jñātvā bhrātṝn punaḥ punaḥ //
1.63.d:
नारदो ऽनुगतान्प्राह पुनस्तान्सूर्यवर्चसः
भुवः प्रमाणं सर्वं तु ज्ञात्वा भ्रातॄन् पुनः पुनः ॥
1.63.m:
Nārada again spoke to those who followed, possessing the splendour of the sun:
“Having known the entire extent of the earth and [found] your brothers,

1.63.s:
āgatya vātha sṛṣṭiṃ vai kariṣyatha viśeṣataḥ
te 'pi tenaiva mārgeṇa jagmurbhrātṛgatiṃ tathā //
1.63.d:
आगत्य वाथ सृष्टिं वै करिष्यथ विशेषतः
ते ऽपि तेनैव मार्गेण जग्मुर्भ्रातृगतिं तथा ॥
1.63.m:
having returned, you will then produce creation in particular.”
They too, along that very path, met with the fate of their brothers.

1.63.s:
tatasteṣvapi naṣṭeṣu ṣaṣṭikanyāḥ prajāpatiḥ
vairiṇyāṃ janayāmāsa dakṣaḥ prācetasastadā //
1.63.d:
ततस्तेष्वपि नष्टेषु षष्टिकन्याः प्रजापतिः
वैरिण्यां जनयामास दक्षः प्राचेतसस्तदा ॥
1.63.m: Then, when they too had vanished, Dakṣa, the lord of creatures, / the son of Pracetas, fathered sixty daughters upon Vairiṇī.

1.63.s:
prādātsa daśakaṃ dharme kaśyapāya trayodaśa
viṃśatsapta ca somāya catasro 'riṣṭanemaye //
1.63.d:
प्रादात्स दशकं धर्मे कश्यपाय त्रयोदश
विंशत्सप्त च सोमाय चतस्रो ऽरिष्टनेमये ॥
1.63.m: He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa, / twenty-seven to Soma, and four to Ariṣṭanemi;

1.63.s:
dve caiva bhṛguputrāya dve kṛśāśvāya dhīmate
dve caivāṅgirase tadvat tāsāṃ nāmāni vistarāt //
1.63.d:
द्वे चैव भृगुपुत्राय द्वे कृशाश्वाय धीमते
द्वे चैवाङ्गिरसे तद्वत् तासां नामानि विस्तरात् ॥
1.63.m: two to the son of Bhṛgu, two to the wise Kṛśāśva, / and likewise two to Aṅgiras. Hear their names in detail,

1.63.s:
śṛṇudhvaṃ devamātṝṇāṃ prajāvistāramāditaḥ
marutvatī vasūr yāmir lambā bhānurarundhatī //
1.63.d:
शृणुध्वं देवमातॄणां प्रजाविस्तारमादितः
मरुत्वती वसूर् यामिर् लम्बा भानुररुन्धती ॥
1.63.m: and the expansion of the offspring of the mothers of the gods from the beginning: / Marutvatī, Vasu, Yāmi, Lambā, Bhānu, Arundhatī,

1.63.s:
saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā ca bhāminī
dharmapatnyaḥ samākhyātās tāsāṃ putrānvadāmi vaḥ //
1.63.d:
संकल्पा च मुहूर्ता च साध्या विश्वा च भामिनी
धर्मपत्न्यः समाख्यातास् तासां पुत्रान्वदामि वः ॥
1.63.m: Saṃkalpā, Muhūrtā, Sādhyā, and the radiant Viśvā / are renowned as the wives of Dharma. I shall tell you their sons.

1.63.s:
viśvedevāstu viśvāyāḥ sādhyā sādhyānajījanat
marutvatyāṃ marutvanto vasostu vasavas tathā //
1.63.d:
विश्वेदेवास्तु विश्वायाः साध्या साध्यानजीजनत्
मरुत्वत्यां मरुत्वन्तो वसोस्तु वसवस् तथा ॥
1.63.m: Viśvā bore the Viśvedevas; Sādhyā gave birth to the Sādhyas; / upon Marutvatī [were born] the Marutvants, and from Vasu the Vasus.

1.63.s:
bhānostu bhānavaḥ proktā muhūrtāyā muhūrtakāḥ
lambāyā ghoṣanāmāno nāgavīthistu yāmijaḥ //
1.63.d:
भानोस्तु भानवः प्रोक्ता मुहूर्ताया मुहूर्तकाः
लम्बाया घोषनामानो नागवीथिस्तु यामिजः ॥
1.63.m: From Bhānu the Bhānus are declared, from Muhūrtā the Muhūrtakas; / Lambā's [sons] are named Ghoṣas, and Nāgavīthi was born of Yāmi.

1.63.s:
saṃkalpāyāstu saṃkalpo vasusargaṃ vadāmi vaḥ
jyotiṣmantastu ye devā vyāpakāḥ sarvatodiśam //
1.63.d:
संकल्पायास्तु संकल्पो वसुसर्गं वदामि वः
ज्योतिष्मन्तस्तु ये देवा व्यापकाः सर्वतोदिशम् ॥
1.63.m: Saṃkalpā's son was Saṃkalpa. I shall tell you the creation of the Vasus: / the radiant gods who pervade all directions,

1.63.s:
vasavaste samākhyātāḥ sarvabhūtahitaiṣiṇaḥ
āpo dhruvaś ca somaś ca dharaścaivānilo 'nalaḥ //
1.63.d:
वसवस्ते समाख्याताः सर्वभूतहितैषिणः
आपो ध्रुवश् च सोमश् च धरश्चैवानिलो ऽनलः ॥
1.63.m: desiring the welfare of all beings, are renowned as the Vasus: / Āpa, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anila, Anala,

1.63.s:
pratyūṣaś ca prabhāsaś ca vasavo 'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ
ajaikapād ahirbudhnyo virūpākṣaḥ sabhairavaḥ //
1.63.d:
प्रत्यूषश् च प्रभासश् च वसवो ऽष्टौ प्रकीर्तिताः
अजैकपाद् अहिर्बुध्न्यो विरूपाक्षः सभैरवः ॥
1.63.m: Pratyūṣa, and Prabhāsa—these are celebrated as the eight Vasus. / Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Virūpākṣa along with Bhairava,

1.63.s:
haraś ca bahurūpaś ca tryaṃbakaś ca sureśvaraḥ
sāvitraś ca jayantaś ca pinākī cāparājitaḥ //
1.63.d:
हरश् च बहुरूपश् च त्र्यंबकश् च सुरेश्वरः
सावित्रश् च जयन्तश् च पिनाकी चापराजितः ॥
1.63.m: Hara, Bahurūpa, Tryambaka, Sureśvara, / Sāvitra, Jayanta, Pinākin, and Aparājita—

1.63.s:
ete rudrāḥ samākhyātā ekādaśa gaṇeśvarāḥ
kaśyapasya pravakṣyāmi patnībhyaḥ putrapautrakam //
1.63.d:
एते रुद्राः समाख्याता एकादश गणेश्वराः
कश्यपस्य प्रवक्ष्यामि पत्नीभ्यः पुत्रपौत्रकम् ॥
1.63.m: these eleven are celebrated as the Rudras, lords of the gaṇas. / I shall [now] declare the sons and grandsons of Kaśyapa by his wives:

1.63.s:
aditiś ca ditiścaiva ariṣṭā surasā muniḥ
surabhir vinatā tāmrā tadvat krodhavaśā ilā //
1.63.d:
अदितिश् च दितिश्चैव अरिष्टा सुरसा मुनिः
सुरभिर् विनता ताम्रा तद्वत् क्रोधवशा इला ॥
1.63.m: Aditi, Diti, Ariṣṭā, Surasā, Muni, / Surabhi, Vinatā, Tāmrā, and likewise Krodhavaśā, Ilā,

1.63.s:
kadrūstviṣā danustadvat tāsāṃ putrānvadāmi vaḥ
tuṣitā nāma ye devāś cākṣuṣasyāntare manoḥ //
1.63.d:
कद्रूस्त्विषा दनुस्तद्वत् तासां पुत्रान्वदामि वः
तुषिता नाम ये देवाश् चाक्षुषस्यान्तरे मनोः ॥
1.63.m: Kadrū, Tviṣā, and Danu. I shall tell you their sons. / The gods named the Tuṣitas in the interval of the Manu Cākṣuṣa

1.63.s:
vaivasvatāntare te vai ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ
indro dhātā bhagastvaṣṭa mitro 'tha varuṇo 'ryamā //
1.63.d:
वैवस्वतान्तरे ते वै आदित्या द्वादश स्मृताः
इन्द्रो धाता भगस्त्वष्ट मित्रो ऽथ वरुणो ऽर्यमा ॥
1.63.m: are indeed remembered as the twelve Ādityas in the interval of Vaivasvata: / Indra, Dhātṛ, Bhaga, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman,

1.63.s:
vivasvānsavitā pūṣā aṃśumān viṣṇureva ca
ete sahasrakiraṇā ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ //
1.63.d:
विवस्वान्सविता पूषा अंशुमान् विष्णुरेव च
एते सहस्रकिरणा आदित्या द्वादश स्मृताः ॥
1.63.m: Vivasvat, Savitṛ, Pūṣan, Aṃśumat, and Viṣṇu. / These thousand-rayed ones are remembered as the twelve Ādityas.

1.63.s:
ditiḥ putradvayaṃ lebhe kaśyapāditi naḥ śrutam
hiraṇyakaśipuṃ caiva hiraṇyākṣaṃ tathaiva ca //
1.63.d:
दितिः पुत्रद्वयं लेभे कश्यपादिति नः श्रुतम्
हिरण्यकशिपुं चैव हिरण्याक्षं तथैव च ॥
1.63.m: Diti obtained two sons from Kaśyapa, as we have heard: / Hiraṇyakaśipu and Hiraṇyākṣa.

1.63.s:
danuḥ putraśataṃ lebhe kaśyapād baladarpitam
vipracittiḥ pradhāno 'bhūt teṣāṃ madhye dvijottamāḥ //
1.63.d:
दनुः पुत्रशतं लेभे कश्यपाद् बलदर्पितम्
विप्रचित्तिः प्रधानो ऽभूत् तेषां मध्ये द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.63.m: Danu obtained from Kaśyapa a hundred sons proud of their strength; / among them Vipracitti became foremost, O best of the twice-born.

1.63.s:
tāmrā ca janayāmāsa ṣaṭ kanyā dvijapuṅgavāḥ
śukīṃ śyenīṃ ca bhāsīṃ ca sugrīvīṃ gṛdhrikāṃ śucim //
1.63.d:
ताम्रा च जनयामास षट् कन्या द्विजपुङ्गवाः
शुकीं श्येनीं च भासीं च सुग्रीवीं गृध्रिकां शुचिम् ॥
1.63.m: Tāmrā gave birth to six daughters, O bulls among the twice-born: / Śukī, Śyenī, Bhāsī, Sugrīvī, Gṛdhrikā, and Śuci.

1.63.s:
śukī śukānulūkāṃś ca janayāmāsa dharmataḥ
śyenī śyenāṃs tathā bhāsī kuraṅgāṃś ca vyajījanat //
1.63.d:
शुकी शुकानुलूकांश् च जनयामास धर्मतः
श्येनी श्येनांस् तथा भासी कुरङ्गांश् च व्यजीजनत् ॥
1.63.m: Śukī rightly gave birth to parrots and owls; / Śyenī gave birth to hawks, and Bhāsī to kites;

1.63.s:
gṛdhrī gṛdhrān kapotāṃś ca pārāvatī vihaṃgamān
haṃsasārasakāraṇḍaplavāñchucirajījanat //
1.63.d:
गृध्री गृध्रान् कपोतांश् च पारावती विहंगमान्
हंससारसकारण्डप्लवाञ्छुचिरजीजनत् ॥
1.63.m: Gṛdhrī [gave birth to] vultures and doves, Pārāvatī to birds, / and Śuci gave birth to swans, sārusa cranes, k系统的araṇḍavas, and ducks.

1.63.s:
ajāśvameṣoṣṭrakharān sugrīvī cāpyajījanat
vinatā janayāmāsa garuḍaṃ cāruṇaṃ śubhā //
1.63.d:
अजाश्वमेषोष्ट्रखरान् सुग्रीवी चाप्यजीजनत्
विनता जनयामास गरुडं चारुणं शुभा ॥
1.63.m: Sugrīvī gave birth to goats, horses, sheep, camels, and donkeys; / the auspicious Vinatā gave birth to Garuḍa and Aruṇa,

1.63.s:
saudāminīṃ tathā kanyāṃ sarvalokabhayaṅkarīm
surasāyāḥ sahasraṃ tu sarpāṇāmabhavatpurā //
1.63.d:
सौदामिनीं तथा कन्यां सर्वलोकभयङ्करीम्
सुरसायाः सहस्रं तु सर्पाणामभवत्पुरा ॥
1.63.m: and also a daughter, Saudāminī, terrifying to all the worlds. / Formerly Surasā had a thousand serpents;

1.63.s:
kadrūḥ sahasraśirasāṃ sahasraṃ prāpa suvratā
pradhānāsteṣu vikhyātāḥ ṣaḍviṃśatiranuttamāḥ //
1.63.d:
कद्रूः सहस्रशिरसां सहस्रं प्राप सुव्रता
प्रधानास्तेषु विख्याताः षड्विंशतिरनुत्तमाः ॥
1.63.m: the faithful Kadrū obtained a thousand thousand-headed [nāgas]. / Twenty-six are celebrated as the foremost and most supreme among them:

1.63.s:
śeṣavāsukikarkoṭaśaṅkhairāvatakambalāḥ
dhanañjayamahānīlapadmāśvataratakṣakāḥ //
1.63.d:
शेषवासुकिकर्कोटशङ्खैरावतकम्बलाः
धनञ्जयमहानीलपद्माश्वतरतक्षकाः ॥
1.63.m: Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Karkoṭa, Śaṅkha, Airāvata, Kambala, / Dhanañjaya, Mahānīla, Padma, Aśvatara, Takṣaka,

1.63.s:
elāpatramahāpadmadhṛtarāṣṭrabalāhakāḥ
śaṅkhapālamahāśaṅkhapuṣpadaṃṣṭraśubhānanāḥ //
1.63.d:
एलापत्रमहापद्मधृतराष्ट्रबलाहकाः
शङ्खपालमहाशङ्खपुष्पदंष्ट्रशुभाननाः ॥
1.63.m: Elāpatra, Mahāpadma, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Balāhaka, / Śaṅkhapāla, Mahāśaṅkha, Puṣpadaṃṣṭra, Śubhānana,

1.63.s:
śaṅkhalomā ca nahuṣo vāmanaḥ phaṇitas tathā
kapilo durmukhaścāpi patañjaliriti smṛtaḥ //
1.63.d:
शङ्खलोमा च नहुषो वामनः फणितस् तथा
कपिलो दुर्मुखश्चापि पतञ्जलिरिति स्मृतः ॥
1.63.m: Śaṅkhaloman, Nahuṣa, Vāmana, Phaṇita, / Kapila, Durmukha, and he who is known as Patañjali.

1.63.s:
rakṣogaṇaṃ krodhavaśā mahāmāyaṃ vyajījanat
rudrāṇāṃ ca gaṇaṃ tadvad gomahiṣyau varāṅganā //
1.63.d:
रक्षोगणं क्रोधवशा महामायं व्यजीजनत्
रुद्राणां च गणं तद्वद् गोमहिष्यौ वराङ्गना ॥
1.63.m: Krodhavaśā gave birth to the horde of Rākṣasas possessing great illusion, / and likewise to the host of Rudras; the excellent woman [Surabhi]

1.63.s:
surabhir janayāmāsa kaśyapāditi naḥ śrutam
munirmunīnāṃ ca gaṇaṃ gaṇamapsarasāṃ tathā //
1.63.d:
सुरभिर् जनयामास कश्यपादिति नः श्रुतम्
मुनिर्मुनीनां च गणं गणमप्सरसां तथा ॥
1.63.m: bore the cow and the buffalo-cow from Kaśyapa, as we have heard. / Muni gave birth to the host of Munis and the host of Apsarases;

1.63.s:
tathā kiṃnaragandharvān ariṣṭājanayadbahūn
tṛṇavṛkṣalatāgulmam ilā sarvamajījanat //
1.63.d:
तथा किंनरगन्धर्वान् अरिष्टाजनयद्बहून्
तृणवृक्षलतागुल्मम् इला सर्वमजीजनत् ॥
1.63.m: Ariṣṭā gave birth to many Kiṃnaras and Gandharvas; / Ilā gave birth to all grass, trees, creepers, and shrubs;

1.63.s:
tviṣā tu yakṣarakṣāṃsi janayāmāsa koṭiśaḥ
ete tu kāśyapeyāś ca saṃkṣepātparikīrtitāḥ //
1.63.d:
त्विषा तु यक्षरक्षांसि जनयामास कोटिशः
एते तु काश्यपेयाश् च संक्षेपात्परिकीर्तिताः ॥
1.63.m: Tviṣā gave birth to Yakṣas and Rākṣasas by the millions. / These descendants of Kaśyapa have been declared in brief.

1.63.s:
eteṣāṃ putrapautrādivaṃśāś ca bahavaḥ smṛtāḥ
evaṃ prajāsu sṛṣṭāsu kaśyapena mahātmanā //
1.63.d:
एतेषां पुत्रपौत्रादिवंशाश् च बहवः स्मृताः
एवं प्रजासु सृष्टासु कश्यपेन महात्मना ॥
1.63.m: Their lineages of sons, grandsons, and so forth are remembered as numerous. / Thus, when all creatures, both moving and unmoving,

1.63.s:
pratiṣṭhitāsu sarvāsu carāsu sthāvarāsu ca
abhiṣicyādhipatyeṣu teṣāṃ mukhyānprajāpatiḥ //
1.63.d:
प्रतिष्ठितासु सर्वासु चरासु स्थावरासु च
अभिषिच्याधिपत्येषु तेषां मुख्यान्प्रजापतिः ॥
1.63.m: had been created by the great-souled Kaśyapa and established, / the lord of creatures, having consecrated their leaders to sovereign positions,

1.63.s:
tato manuṣyādhipatiṃ cakre vaivasvataṃ manum
svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare pūrvaṃ brahmaṇā ye 'bhiṣecitāḥ //
1.63.d:
ततो मनुष्याधिपतिं चक्रे वैवस्वतं मनुम्
स्वायंभुवे ऽन्तरे पूर्वं ब्रह्मणा ये ऽभिषेचिताः ॥
1.63.m: then made Vaivasvata Manu the ruler of humans. / Those who were consecrated by Brahmā in the ancient Svāyambhuva interval—

1.63.s:
tairiyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā saptadvīpā saparvatā
yathopadeśamadyāpi dharmeṇa pratipālyate //
1.63.d:
तैरियं पृथिवी सर्वा सप्तद्वीपा सपर्वता
यथोपदेशमद्यापि धर्मेण प्रतिपाल्यते ॥
1.63.m: by them this entire earth with its seven continents and mountains / is guarded righteously according to instruction even today.

1.63.s:
svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare pūrve brahmaṇā ye 'bhiṣecitāḥ
te hyete cābhiṣicyante manavaś ca bhavanti te //
1.63.d:
स्वायंभुवे ऽन्तरे पूर्वे ब्रह्मणा ये ऽभिषेचिताः
ते ह्येते चाभिषिच्यन्ते मनवश् च भवन्ति ते ॥
1.63.m: Those who were consecrated by Brahmā in the former Svāyambhuva interval, / these are indeed consecrated and become the Manus.

1.63.s:
manvantareṣvatīteṣu gatā hyeteṣu pārthivāḥ
evamanye 'bhiṣicyante prāpte manvantare tataḥ //
1.63.d:
मन्वन्तरेष्वतीतेषु गता ह्येतेषु पार्थिवाः
एवमन्ये ऽभिषिच्यन्ते प्राप्ते मन्वन्तरे ततः ॥
1.63.m: When the manvantaras pass away, these kings depart; / thus others are consecrated when that manvantara arrives.

1.63.s:
atītānāgatāḥ sarve nṛpā manvantare smṛtāḥ
etānutpādya putrāṃstu prajāsaṃtānakāraṇāt //
1.63.d:
अतीतानागताः सर्वे नृपा मन्वन्तरे स्मृताः
एतानुत्पाद्य पुत्रांस्तु प्रजासंतानकारणात् ॥
1.63.m: All past and future kings in a manvantara are remembered [in this way]. / Having generated these sons for the continuation of offspring,

1.63.s:
kaśyapo gotrakāmastu cacāra sa punastapaḥ
putro gotrakaro mahyaṃ bhavatād iti cintayan //
1.63.d:
कश्यपो गोत्रकामस्तु चचार स पुनस्तपः
पुत्रो गोत्रकरो मह्यं भवताद् इति चिन्तयन् ॥
1.63.m: Kaśyapa, desiring a gotra, performed austerities once more, / thinking: “May a son who establishes my gotra be born to me.”

1.63.s:
tasyaivaṃ dhyāyamānasya kaśyapasya mahātmanaḥ
brahmayogātsutau paścāt prādurbhūtau mahaujasau //
1.63.d:
तस्यैवं ध्यायमानस्य कश्यपस्य महात्मनः
ब्रह्मयोगात्सुतौ पश्चात् प्रादुर्भूतौ महौजसौ ॥
1.63.m: As the great-souled Kaśyapa was thus meditating, / two sons of great splendour were subsequently born through brahmayoga:

1.63.s:
vatsaraścāsitaścaiva tāvubhau brahmavādinau
vatsarānnaidhruvo jajñe raibhyaś ca sumahāyaśāḥ //
1.63.d:
वत्सरश्चासितश्चैव तावुभौ ब्रह्मवादिनौ
वत्सरान्नैध्रुवो जज्ञे रैभ्यश् च सुमहायशाः ॥
1.63.m: Vatsara and Asita, both expositors of the Veda. / From Vatsara was born Naidhruva, and Raibhya of exceedingly great renown.

1.63.s:
raibhyasya raibhyā vijñeyā naidhruvasya vadāmi vaḥ
cyavanasya tu kanyāyāṃ sumedhāḥ samapadyata //
1.63.d:
रैभ्यस्य रैभ्या विज्ञेया नैध्रुवस्य वदामि वः
च्यवनस्य तु कन्यायां सुमेधाः समपद्यत ॥
1.63.m: Raibhya's descendants are known as the Raibhyas; I shall tell you of Naidhruva: / on the daughter of Cyavana, Sumedhas was born.

1.63.s:
naidhruvasya tu sā patnī mātā vai kuṇḍapāyinām
asitasyaikaparṇāyāṃ brahmiṣṭhaḥ samapadyata //
1.63.d:
नैध्रुवस्य तु सा पत्नी माता वै कुण्डपायिनाम्
असितस्यैकपर्णायां ब्रह्मिष्ठः समपद्यत ॥
1.63.m: She was the wife of Naidhruva and the mother of the Kuṇḍapāyins. / On Ekaparṇā, Asita fathered the most devoted to Brahman,

1.63.s:
śāṇḍilyānāṃ varaḥ śrīmān devalaḥ sumahātapāḥ
śāṇḍilyā naidhruvā raibhyās trayaḥ pakṣāstu kāśyapāḥ //
1.63.d:
शाण्डिल्यानां वरः श्रीमान् देवलः सुमहातपाः
शाण्डिल्या नैध्रुवा रैभ्यास् त्रयः पक्षास्तु काश्यपाः ॥
1.63.m: the eminent and glorious Devala of exceedingly great austerities. / The Śāṇḍilyas, the Naidhruvas, and the Raibhyas are the three branches of Kaśyapa.

1.63.s:
nava prakṛtayo devāḥ pulastyasya vadāmi vaḥ
caturyuge hyatikrānte manorekādaśe prabhoḥ //
1.63.d:
नव प्रकृतयो देवाः पुलस्त्यस्य वदामि वः
चतुर्युगे ह्यतिक्रान्ते मनोरेकादशे प्रभोः ॥
1.63.m: I shall tell you of the nine original deities of Pulastya: / when a four-yuga cycle had passed in the eleventh [interval of] Manu of the Lord,

1.63.s:
ardhāvaśiṣṭe tasmiṃstu dvāpare sampravartite
mānavasya nariṣyantaḥ putra āsīd damaḥ kila //
1.63.d:
अर्धावशिष्टे तस्मिंस्तु द्वापरे सम्प्रवर्तिते
मानवस्य नरिष्यन्तः पुत्र आसीद् दमः किल ॥
1.63.m: when half remained and that Dvāpara had begun, / Nariṣyanta, a descendant of Manu, had a son named Dama, it is said.

1.63.s:
damasya tasya dāyādas tṛṇabinduriti smṛtaḥ
tretāyugamukhe rājā tṛtīye saṃbabhūva ha //
1.63.d:
दमस्य तस्य दायादस् तृणबिन्दुरिति स्मृतः
त्रेतायुगमुखे राजा तृतीये संबभूव ह ॥
1.63.m: The heir of that Dama is remembered as Tṛṇabindu; / he became king at the beginning of the third Tretāyuga.

1.63.s:
tasya kanyā tvilavilā rūpeṇāpratimābhavat
pulastyāya sa rājarṣis tāṃ kanyāṃ pratyapādayat //
1.63.d:
तस्य कन्या त्विलविला रूपेणाप्रतिमाभवत्
पुलस्त्याय स राजर्षिस् तां कन्यां प्रत्यपादयत् ॥
1.63.m: His daughter was Ilavilā, who was peerless in beauty; / that royal sage gave that maiden to Pulastya.

1.63.s:
ṛṣir airavilo yasyāṃ viśravāḥ samapadyata
tasya patnyaścatasrastu paulastyakulavardhanāḥ //
1.63.d:
ऋषिर् ऐरविलो यस्यां विश्रवाः समपद्यत
तस्य पत्न्यश्चतस्रस्तु पौलस्त्यकुलवर्धनाः ॥
1.63.m: Upon her was born the sage Viśravas, son of Ilavilā. / He had four wives who expanded the family of Pulastya.

1.63.s:
bṛhaspateḥ śubhā kanyā nāmnā vai devavarṇinī
puṣpotkaṭā balākā ca sute mālyavataḥ smṛteḥ //
1.63.d:
बृहस्पतेः शुभा कन्या नाम्ना वै देववर्णिनी
पुष्पोत्कटा बलाका च सुते माल्यवतः स्मृतेः ॥
1.63.m: The auspicious daughter of Bṛhaspati named Devavarṇinī, / and Puṣpotkaṭā and Balākā, remembered as the daughters of Mālyavat,

1.63.s:
kaikasī mālinaḥ kanyā tāsāṃ vai śṛṇuta prajāḥ
jyeṣṭhaṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ tasmāt suṣuve devavarṇinī //
1.63.d:
कैकसी मालिनः कन्या तासां वै शृणुत प्रजाः
ज्येष्ठं वैश्रवणं तस्मात् सुषुवे देववर्णिनी ॥
1.63.m: and Kaikasī, daughter of Mālin: hear about their offspring! / From him, Devavarṇinī gave birth first to the eldest, Vaiśravaṇa.

1.63.s:
kaikasī cāpyajanayad rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam
kumbhakarṇaṃ śūrpaṇakhāṃ dhīmantaṃ ca vibhīṣaṇam //
1.63.d:
कैकसी चाप्यजनयद् रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्
कुम्भकर्णं शूर्पणखां धीमन्तं च विभीषणम् ॥
1.63.m: And Kaikasī gave birth to Rāvaṇa, the lord of the rākṣasas, / Kumbhakarṇa, Śūrpaṇakhā, and the wise Vibhīṣaṇa.

1.63.s:
puṣpotkaṭā hyajanayat putrāṃstasmāddvijottamāḥ
mahodaraṃ prahastaṃ ca mahāpārśvaṃ kharaṃ tathā //
1.63.d:
पुष्पोत्कटा ह्यजनयत् पुत्रांस्तस्माद्द्विजोत्तमाः
महोदरं प्रहस्तं च महापार्श्वं खरं तथा ॥
1.63.m: Puṣpotkaṭā bore sons from him, O best of the twice-born: / Mahodara, Prahasta, Mahāpārśva, and Khara,

1.63.s:
kumbhīnasīṃ tathā kanyāṃ balāyāḥ śṛṇuta prajāḥ
triśirā dūṣaṇaścaiva vidyujjihvaś ca rākṣasaḥ //
1.63.d:
कुम्भीनसीं तथा कन्यां बलायाः शृणुत प्रजाः
त्रिशिरा दूषणश्चैव विद्युज्जिह्वश् च राक्षसः ॥
1.63.m: and a daughter, Kumbhīnasī. Hear the offspring of Balā: / Triśiras, Dūṣaṇa, and the rākṣasa Vidyujjihva,

1.63.s:
kanyā vai mālikā cāpi balāyāḥ prasavaḥ smṛtaḥ
ityete krūrakarmāṇaḥ paulastyā rākṣasā nava //
1.63.d:
कन्या वै मालिका चापि बलायाः प्रसवः स्मृतः
इत्येते क्रूरकर्माणः पौलस्त्या राक्षसा नव ॥
1.63.m: and the daughter Mālikā is remembered as Balā's issue. / These are the nine rākṣasas of cruel deeds born in Pulastya's line.

1.63.s:
vibhīṣaṇo 'tiśuddhātmā dharmajñaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
pulastyasya mṛgāḥ putrāḥ sarve vyāghrāś ca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ //
1.63.d:
विभीषणो ऽतिशुद्धात्मा धर्मज्ञः परिकीर्तितः
पुलस्त्यस्य मृगाः पुत्राः सर्वे व्याघ्राश् च दंष्ट्रिणः ॥
1.63.m: Vibhīṣaṇa is celebrated as one of exceedingly pure soul, knower of dharma. / Deer are the sons of Pulastya, and all tigers and fanged beasts,

1.63.s:
bhūtāḥ piśācāḥ sarpāś ca sūkarā hastinas tathā
vānarāḥ kiṃnarāścaiva ye ca kiṃpuruṣās tathā //
1.63.d:
भूताः पिशाचाः सर्पाश् च सूकरा हस्तिनस् तथा
वानराः किंनराश्चैव ये च किंपुरुषास् तथा ॥
1.63.m: bhūtas, piśācas, snakes, boars, and elephants, / monkeys, kiṃnaras, and kimpuruṣas.

1.63.s:
anapatyaḥ kratustasmin smṛto vaivasvate 'ntare
atreḥ patnyo daśaivāsan suṃdaryaś ca pativratāḥ //
1.63.d:
अनपत्यः क्रतुस्तस्मिन् स्मृतो वैवस्वते ऽन्तरे
अत्रेः पत्न्यो दशैवासन् सुंदर्यश् च पतिव्रताः ॥
1.63.m: Kratu is remembered as childless in that Vaivasvata interval. / Atri had ten beautiful and devoted wives,

1.63.s:
bhadrāśvasya ghṛtācyāṃ vai daśāpsarasi sūnavaḥ
bhadrābhadrā ca jaladā mandā nandā tathaiva ca //
1.63.d:
भद्राश्वस्य घृताच्यां वै दशाप्सरसि सूनवः
भद्राभद्रा च जलदा मन्दा नन्दा तथैव च ॥
1.63.m: daughters of Bhadrāśva born from the apsaras Ghṛtācī: / Bhadrā, Bhadrā, Jaladā, Mandā, Nandā,

1.63.s:
balābalā ca viprendrā yā ca gopābalā smṛtā
tathā tāmarasā caiva varakrīḍā ca vai daśa //
1.63.d:
बलाबला च विप्रेन्द्रा या च गोपाबला स्मृता
तथा तामरसा चैव वरक्रीडा च वै दश ॥
1.63.m: Balābalā, O foremost of vipras, and she who is known as Gopābalā, / as well as Tāmarasā and Varakrīḍā—these ten.

1.63.s:
ātreyavaṃśaprabhavās tāsāṃ bhartā prabhākaraḥ
svarbhānupihite sūrye patite 'smindivo mahīm //
1.63.d:
आत्रेयवंशप्रभवास् तासां भर्ता प्रभाकरः
स्वर्भानुपिहिते सूर्ये पतिते ऽस्मिन्दिवो महीम् ॥
1.63.m: The husband of those women, who produced the line of Ātreyas, was Prabhākara. / When the sun was obscured by Svarbhānu and fell from heaven to the earth,

1.63.s:
tamo 'bhibhūte loke 'smin prabhā yena pravartitā
svastyastu hi tavetyukte patanniha divākaraḥ //
1.63.d:
तमो ऽभिभूते लोके ऽस्मिन् प्रभा येन प्रवर्तिता
स्वस्त्यस्तु हि तवेत्युक्ते पतन्निह दिवाकरः ॥
1.63.m: when this world was overcome by darkness, by him radiance was brought forth. / When he said, 'May it be well with you,' as the sun was falling here,

1.63.s:
brahmarṣervacanāttasya papāta na vibhurdivaḥ
tataḥ prabhākaretyuktaḥ prabhuratrirmaharṣibhiḥ //
1.63.d:
ब्रह्मर्षेर्वचनात्तस्य पपात न विभुर्दिवः
ततः प्रभाकरेत्युक्तः प्रभुरत्रिर्महर्षिभिः ॥
1.63.m: by the word of that brahmarṣi, the powerful one did not fall from heaven. / Therefore the powerful Atri was called 'Prabhākara' by the great rṣis.

1.63.s:
bhadrāyāṃ janayāmāsa somaṃ putraṃ yaśasvinam
sa tāsu janayāmāsa punaḥ putrāṃstapodhanaḥ //
1.63.d:
भद्रायां जनयामास सोमं पुत्रं यशस्विनम्
स तासु जनयामास पुनः पुत्रांस्तपोधनः ॥
1.63.m: On Bhadrā he begot a son, the renowned Soma. / Then that ascetic again begot sons on those women,

1.63.s:
svastyātreyā iti khyātā ṛṣayo vedapāragāḥ
teṣāṃ dvau khyātayaśasau brahmiṣṭhau ca mahaujasau //
1.63.d:
स्वस्त्यात्रेया इति ख्याता ऋषयो वेदपारगाः
तेषां द्वौ ख्यातयशसौ ब्रह्मिष्ठौ च महौजसौ ॥
1.63.m: renowned as the Svastyātreyas, rṣis who had crossed to the other shore of the Vedas. / Among them two were of renowned fame, most devoted to Brahman and of great vigor:

1.63.s:
datto hyatrivaro jyeṣṭho durvāsāstasya cānujaḥ
yavīyasī svasā teṣām amalā brahmavādinī //
1.63.d:
दत्तो ह्यत्रिवरो ज्येष्ठो दुर्वासास्तस्य चानुजः
यवीयसी स्वसा तेषाम् अमला ब्रह्मवादिनी ॥
1.63.m: Datta, the foremost of Atri's line, the eldest, and Durvāsas, his younger brother; / their youngest sister was pure and a proclaimer of Brahman.

1.63.s:
tasya gotradvaye jātāś catvāraḥ prathitā bhuvi
śyāvaś ca pratvasaścaiva vavalguścātha gahvaraḥ //
1.63.d:
तस्य गोत्रद्वये जाताश् चत्वारः प्रथिता भुवि
श्यावश् च प्रत्वसश्चैव ववल्गुश्चाथ गह्वरः ॥
1.63.m: In his two gotras four were born, celebrated upon the earth: / Śyāva, Pratvasa, Vavalgu, and Gahvara.

1.63.s:
ātreyāṇāṃ ca catvāraḥ smṛtāḥ pakṣā mahātmanām
kāśyapo nāradaścaiva parvatānuddhatas tathā //
1.63.d:
आत्रेयाणां च चत्वारः स्मृताः पक्षा महात्मनाम्
काश्यपो नारदश्चैव पर्वतानुद्धतस् तथा ॥
1.63.m: And four branches of the high-souled Ātreyas are remembered. / Kāśyapa, Nārada, Parvata, and Anuddhata—

1.63.s:
jajñire mānasā hyete arundhatyā nibodhata
nāradastu vasiṣṭhāyā-rundhatīṃ pratyapādayat //
1.63.d:
जज्ञिरे मानसा ह्येते अरुन्धत्या निबोधत
नारदस्तु वसिष्ठाया-रुन्धतीं प्रत्यपादयत् ॥
1.63.m: these were indeed born as the mind-born sons of Arundhatī; understand this! / But Nārada bestowed Arundhatī upon Vasiṣṭha.

1.63.s:
ūrdhvaretā mahātejā dakṣaśāpāttu nāradaḥ
purā devāsure yuddhe ghore vai tārakāmaye //
1.63.d:
ऊर्ध्वरेता महातेजा दक्षशापात्तु नारदः
पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे घोरे वै तारकामये ॥
1.63.m: Nārada, of great splendour, was celibate due to the curse of Dakṣa. / Formerly, in the dreadful Tārakāmaya war between gods and asuras,

1.63.s:
anāvṛṣṭyā hate loke hy ugre lokeśvaraiḥ saha
vasiṣṭhastapasā dhīmān dhārayāmāsa vai prajāḥ //
1.63.d:
अनावृष्ट्या हते लोके ह्य् उग्रे लोकेश्वरैः सह
वसिष्ठस्तपसा धीमान् धारयामास वै प्रजाः ॥
1.63.m: when the world was destroyed by a severe drought along with the world-protectors, / the wise Vasiṣṭha sustained the creatures by his tapas,

1.63.s:
annodakaṃ mūlaphalam oṣadhīś ca pravartayan
tānetāñjīvayāmāsa kāruṇyādauṣadhena ca //
1.63.d:
अन्नोदकं मूलफलम् ओषधीश् च प्रवर्तयन्
तानेताञ्जीवयामास कारुण्यादौषधेन च ॥
1.63.m: bringing forth food and water, roots, fruits, and medicinal plants; / out of compassion he revived them with healing herbs.

1.63.s:
arundhatyāṃ vasiṣṭhastu sutān utpādayacchatam
jyāyaso 'janayacchakter adṛśyantī parāśaram //
1.63.d:
अरुन्धत्यां वसिष्ठस्तु सुतान् उत्पादयच्छतम्
ज्यायसो ऽजनयच्छक्तेर् अदृश्यन्ती पराशरम् ॥
1.63.m: And Vasiṣṭha begot a hundred sons on Arundhatī. / On the eldest, Śakti, Adṛśyantī gave birth to Parāśara.

1.63.s:
rakṣasā bhakṣite śaktau rudhireṇa tu vai tadā
kālī parāśarājjajñe kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ prabhum //
1.63.d:
रक्षसा भक्षिते शक्तौ रुधिरेण तु वै तदा
काली पराशराज्जज्ञे कृष्णद्वैपायनं प्रभुम् ॥
1.63.m: When Śakti was devoured by the rākṣasa Rudhira, / Kālī then gave birth to the lord Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana from Parāśara.

1.63.s:
dvaipāyano hyaraṇyāṃ vai śukam utpādayatsutam
upamanyuṃ ca pīvaryāṃ viddhīme śukasūnavaḥ //
1.63.d:
द्वैपायनो ह्यरण्यां वै शुकम् उत्पादयत्सुतम्
उपमन्युं च पीवर्यां विद्धीमे शुकसूनवः ॥
1.63.m: Dvaipāyana begot the son Śuka on the fire-drill; / and know these as the sons of Śuka born on Pīvarī:

1.63.s:
bhūriśravāḥ prabhuḥ śaṃbhuḥ kṛṣṇo gaurastu pañcamaḥ
kanyā kīrtimatī caiva yogamātā dhṛtavratā //
1.63.d:
भूरिश्रवाः प्रभुः शंभुः कृष्णो गौरस्तु पञ्चमः
कन्या कीर्तिमती चैव योगमाता धृतव्रता ॥
1.63.m: Bhūriśravas, the lord Śambhu, Kṛṣṇa, and Gaura as the fifth, / and the daughter Kīrtimatī, mother of yoga, firm in her vows,

1.63.s:
jananī brahmadattasya patnī sā tvanuhasya ca
śvetaḥ kṛṣṇaś ca gauraś ca śyāmo dhūmrastathāruṇaḥ //
1.63.d:
जननी ब्रह्मदत्तस्य पत्नी सा त्वनुहस्य च
श्वेतः कृष्णश् च गौरश् च श्यामो धूम्रस्तथारुणः ॥
1.63.m: the mother of Brahmadatta and wife of Anuha. / Śveta, Kṛṣṇa, Gaura, Śyāma, Dhūmra, Aruṇa,

1.63.s:
nīlo bādarikaścaiva sarve caite parāśarāḥ
parāśarāṇāmaṣṭau te pakṣāḥ proktā mahātmanām //
1.63.d:
नीलो बादरिकश्चैव सर्वे चैते पराशराः
पराशराणामष्टौ ते पक्षाः प्रोक्ता महात्मनाम् ॥
1.63.m: Nīla, and Bādarika: all these are Parāśaras. / These are declared to be the eight branches of the high-souled Parāśaras.

1.63.s:
ata ūrdhvaṃ nibodhadhvam indrapramitisaṃbhavam
vasiṣṭhasya kapiñjalyo ghṛtācyāmudapadyata //
1.63.d:
अत ऊर्ध्वं निबोधध्वम् इन्द्रप्रमितिसंभवम्
वसिष्ठस्य कपिञ्जल्यो घृताच्यामुदपद्यत ॥
1.63.m: Hereafter, learn about the descent of Indrapramiti: / from Vasiṣṭha, Kapiñjalī was born on Ghṛtācī,

1.63.s:
trimūrtiryaḥ samākhyāta indrapramitirucyate
pṛthoḥ sutāyāṃ sambhūto bhadrastasyā bhavadvasuḥ //
1.63.d:
त्रिमूर्तिर्यः समाख्यात इन्द्रप्रमितिरुच्यते
पृथोः सुतायां सम्भूतो भद्रस्तस्या भवद्वसुः ॥
1.63.m: who is proclaimed as Trimūrti and called Indrapramiti. / Born of the daughter of Pṛthu, his son was Bhadravasu.

1.63.s:
upamanyuḥ sutastasya bahavo hyaupamanyavaḥ
mitrāvaruṇayoścaiva kauṇḍinyā ye pariśrutāḥ //
1.63.d:
उपमन्युः सुतस्तस्य बहवो ह्यौपमन्यवः
मित्रावरुणयोश्चैव कौण्डिन्या ये परिश्रुताः ॥
1.63.m: His son was Upamanyu, and numerous are the Aupamanyavas. / And those celebrated as Kauṇḍinyas of Mitra and Varuṇa,

1.63.s:
ekārṣeyās tathā cānye vāsiṣṭhā nāma viśrutāḥ
ete pakṣā vasiṣṭhānāṃ smṛtā daśa mahātmanām //
1.63.d:
एकार्षेयास् तथा चान्ये वासिष्ठा नाम विश्रुताः
एते पक्षा वसिष्ठानां स्मृता दश महात्मनाम् ॥
1.63.m: and others known as the Ekārṣeya Vāsiṣṭhas: / these are remembered as the ten branches of the high-souled descendants of Vasiṣṭha.

1.63.s:
ityete brahmaṇaḥ putrā mānasā viśrutā bhuvi
bhartāraś ca mahābhāgā eṣāṃ vaṃśāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //
1.63.d:
इत्येते ब्रह्मणः पुत्रा मानसा विश्रुता भुवि
भर्तारश् च महाभागा एषां वंशाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
1.63.m: These are the mind-born sons of Brahmā celebrated on earth, / and the illustrious protectors whose lineages have been proclaimed,

1.63.s:
trilokadhāraṇe śaktā devarṣikulasaṃbhavāḥ
teṣāṃ putrāś ca pautrāś ca śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ //
1.63.d:
त्रिलोकधारणे शक्ता देवर्षिकुलसंभवाः
तेषां पुत्राश् च पौत्राश् च शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
1.63.m: capable of sustaining the three worlds, originating from the line of devarṣis. / Their sons and grandsons, in hundreds and thousands,

1.63.s: yaistu vyāptāstrayo lokāḥ sūryasyeva gabhastibhiḥ //
1.63.d: यैस्तु व्याप्तास्त्रयो लोकाः सूर्यस्येव गभस्तिभिः ॥
1.63.m: pervade the three worlds like the rays of the sun.

1.64.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
kathaṃ hi rakṣasā śaktir bhakṣitaḥ so 'nujaiḥ saha
vāsiṣṭho vadatāṃ śreṣṭha sūta vaktumihārhasi //
1.64.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
कथं हि रक्षसा शक्तिर् भक्षितः सो ऽनुजैः सह
वासिष्ठो वदतां श्रेष्ठ सूत वक्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
1.64.m: The rṣis said: / How indeed was Śakti, the son of Vasiṣṭha, devoured by a rākṣasa along with his younger brothers? / O Sūta, best of speakers, you ought to tell this here.

1.64.s:
sūta uvāca
rākṣaso rudhiro nāma vasiṣṭhasya sutaṃ purā
śaktiṃ sa bhakṣayāmāsa śakteḥ śāpātsahānujaiḥ //
1.64.d:
सूत उवाच
राक्षसो रुधिरो नाम वसिष्ठस्य सुतं पुरा
शक्तिं स भक्षयामास शक्तेः शापात्सहानुजैः ॥
1.64.m: Sūta said: / Formerly, a rākṣasa named Rudhira devoured Śakti, / the son of Vasiṣṭha, along with his younger brothers, because of Śakti's curse.

1.64.s:
vasiṣṭhayājyaṃ viprendrās tadādiśyaiva bhūpatim
kalmāṣapādaṃ rudhiro viśvāmitreṇa coditaḥ //
1.64.d:
वसिष्ठयाज्यं विप्रेन्द्रास् तदादिश्यैव भूपतिम्
कल्माषपादं रुधिरो विश्वामित्रेण चोदितः ॥
1.64.m: Having then appointed King Kalmāṣapāda, the patron of Vasiṣṭha's sacrifice, O foremost vipras, / Rudhira was impelled by Viśvāmitra.

1.64.s:
bhakṣitaḥ sa iti śrutvā vasiṣṭhastena rakṣasā
śaktiḥ śaktimatāṃ śreṣṭho bhrātṛbhiḥ saha dharmavit //
1.64.d:
भक्षितः स इति श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठस्तेन रक्षसा
शक्तिः शक्तिमतां श्रेष्ठो भ्रातृभिः सह धर्मवित् ॥
1.64.m: Hearing that he, Śakti, the foremost of the capable and knower of dharma, / had been devoured by that rākṣasa together with his brothers,

1.64.s:
hā putra putra putreti krandamāno muhurmuhuḥ
arundhatyā saha muniḥ papāta bhuvi duḥkhitaḥ //
1.64.d:
हा पुत्र पुत्र पुत्रेति क्रन्दमानो मुहुर्मुहुः
अरुन्धत्या सह मुनिः पपात भुवि दुःखितः ॥
1.64.m: crying out again and again, 'Alas, my son! My son! My son!' / the sage, stricken with grief, fell to the earth along with Arundhatī.

1.64.s:
naṣṭaṃ kulamiti śrutvā martuṃ cakre matiṃ tadā
smaranputraśataṃ caiva śaktijyeṣṭhaṃ ca śaktimān //
1.64.d:
नष्टं कुलमिति श्रुत्वा मर्तुं चक्रे मतिं तदा
स्मरन्पुत्रशतं चैव शक्तिज्येष्ठं च शक्तिमान् ॥
1.64.m: Hearing that his family was destroyed, he then resolved to die, / remembering his hundred sons with Śakti as the eldest, the capable one.

1.64.s: na taṃ vināhaṃ jīviṣye iti niścitya duḥkhitaḥ //
1.64.d: न तं विनाहं जीविष्ये इति निश्चित्य दुःखितः ॥
1.64.m: Determining in his grief, 'I shall not live without him,'

1.64.s:
āruhya mūrdhānam ajātmajo 'sau tayātmavān sarvavid ātmavicca
dharādharasyaiva tadā dharāyāṃ papāta patnyā saha sāśrudṛṣṭiḥ //
1.64.d:
आरुह्य मूर्धानम् अजात्मजो ऽसौ तयात्मवान् सर्वविद् आत्मविच्च
धराधरस्यैव तदा धरायां पपात पत्न्या सह साश्रुदृष्टिः ॥
1.64.m: that self-controlled son of the Unborn [Brahmā], knower of all and knower of the Self, / climbed the summit of a mountain and fell to the earth with his wife, eyes filled with tears.

1.64.s:
dharādharāttaṃ patitaṃ dharā tadā dadhāra tatrāpi vicitrakaṇṭhī
karāṃbujābhyāṃ karikhelagāminī rudantamādāya ruroda sā ca //
1.64.d:
धराधरात्तं पतितं धरा तदा दधार तत्रापि विचित्रकण्ठी
करांबुजाभ्यां करिखेलगामिनी रुदन्तमादाय रुरोद सा च ॥
1.64.m: The earth then caught him as he fell from the mountain; and there, she of lovely voice, / who moved like a playful elephant, took him in her lotus hands as he wept, and she too wept.

1.64.s:
tadā tasya snuṣā prāha patnī śaktermahāmunim
vasiṣṭhaṃ vadatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ rudantī bhayavihvalā //
1.64.d:
तदा तस्य स्नुषा प्राह पत्नी शक्तेर्महामुनिम्
वसिष्ठं वदतां श्रेष्ठं रुदन्ती भयविह्वला ॥
1.64.m: Then his daughter-in-law, the wife of Śakti, weeping and overwhelmed by fear, / spoke to that great sage Vasiṣṭha, the best of speakers:

1.64.s:
bhagavanbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭha tava deham idaṃ śubham
pālayasva vibho draṣṭuṃ tava pautraṃ mamātmajam //
1.64.d:
भगवन्ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठ तव देहम् इदं शुभम्
पालयस्व विभो द्रष्टुं तव पौत्रं ममात्मजम् ॥
1.64.m: O venerable one, best of brāhmaṇas, preserve this auspicious body of yours, / O lord, to behold your grandson, my son!

1.64.s:
na tyājyaṃ tava viprendra dehametatsuśobhanam
garbhastho mama sarvārthasādhakaḥ śaktijo yataḥ //
1.64.d:
न त्याज्यं तव विप्रेन्द्र देहमेतत्सुशोभनम्
गर्भस्थो मम सर्वार्थसाधकः शक्तिजो यतः ॥
1.64.m: "You must not abandon this most auspicious body of yours, O best of Brahmins, / for within my womb rests the son of Śakti, who accomplishes all aims."

1.64.s:
evamuktvātha dharmajñā karābhyāṃ kamalekṣaṇā
utthāpya śvaśuraṃ natvā netre saṃmṛjya vāriṇā //
1.64.d:
एवमुक्त्वाथ धर्मज्ञा कराभ्यां कमलेक्षणा
उत्थाप्य श्वशुरं नत्वा नेत्रे संमृज्य वारिणा ॥
1.64.m: Having spoken thus, the lotus-eyed woman, knower of dharma, / raised her father-in-law with both hands, bowed to him, wiped her eyes with water,

1.64.s:
duḥkhitāpi paritrātuṃ śvaśuraṃ duḥkhitaṃ tadā
arundhatīṃ ca kalyāṇīṃ prārthayāmāsa duḥkhitām //
1.64.d:
दुःखितापि परित्रातुं श्वशुरं दुःखितं तदा
अरुन्धतीं च कल्याणीं प्रार्थयामास दुःखिताम् ॥
1.64.m: and, though sorrowful herself, then prayed to protect her grieving father-in-law / and the auspicious, sorrowing Arundhatī.

1.64.s:
snuṣāvākyaṃ tataḥ śrutvā vasiṣṭha utthāya bhūtalāt
saṃjñāmavāpya cāliṅgya sā papāta suduḥkhitā //
1.64.d:
स्नुषावाक्यं ततः श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठ उत्थाय भूतलात्
संज्ञामवाप्य चालिङ्ग्य सा पपात सुदुःखिता ॥
1.64.m: Then, hearing the words of his daughter-in-law, Vasiṣṭha rose from the ground; / recovering consciousness and embracing her, she fell down in deep sorrow.

1.64.s:
arundhatī karābhyāṃ tāṃ saṃspṛśyāsrākulekṣaṇām
ruroda muniśārdūlo bhāryayā sutavatsalaḥ //
1.64.d:
अरुन्धती कराभ्यां तां संस्पृश्यास्राकुलेक्षणाम्
रुरोद मुनिशार्दूलो भार्यया सुतवत्सलः ॥
1.64.m: Touching her with both hands as her eyes were troubled with tears, Arundhatī [wept]; / and the tiger among sages, loving his son, wept together with his wife.

1.64.s:
atha nābhyaṃbuje viṣṇor yathā tasyāścaturmukhaḥ
āsīno garbhaśayyāyāṃ kumāra ṛcamāha saḥ //
1.64.d:
अथ नाभ्यंबुजे विष्णोर् यथा तस्याश्चतुर्मुखः
आसीनो गर्भशय्यायां कुमार ऋचमाह सः ॥
1.64.m: Then, just as the four-faced [Brahmā] sat upon Viṣṇu's navel-lotus, / the child, seated upon the bed of her womb, recited an Ṛg-verse.

1.64.s:
tato niśamya bhagavān vasiṣṭha ṛcamādarāt
kenoktamiti saṃcintya tadātiṣṭhatsamāhitaḥ //
1.64.d:
ततो निशम्य भगवान् वसिष्ठ ऋचमादरात्
केनोक्तमिति संचिन्त्य तदातिष्ठत्समाहितः ॥
1.64.m: Hearing that Ṛg-verse with reverence, the lord Vasiṣṭha / then stood focused, pondering: "By whom was this uttered?"

1.64.s:
vyomāṅgaṇastho 'tha hariḥ puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇaḥ
vasiṣṭhamāha viśvātmā ghṛṇayā sa ghṛṇānidhiḥ //
1.64.d:
व्योमाङ्गणस्थो ऽथ हरिः पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणः
वसिष्ठमाह विश्वात्मा घृणया स घृणानिधिः ॥
1.64.m: Then Hari, whose eyes resemble a white lotus, standing in the courtyard of the sky, / the Self of the universe and a treasury of compassion, spoke with compassion to Vasiṣṭha:

1.64.s:
bho vatsa vatsa viprendra vasiṣṭha sutavatsala
tava pautramukhāmbhojād ṛg eṣādya viniḥsṛtā //
1.64.d:
भो वत्स वत्स विप्रेन्द्र वसिष्ठ सुतवत्सल
तव पौत्रमुखाम्भोजाद् ऋग् एषाद्य विनिःसृता ॥
1.64.m: "O child, child, best of Brahmins, Vasiṣṭha, lover of your son! / From your grandson's lotus-mouth this Ṛg-verse has issued today.

1.64.s:
matsamastava pautro 'sau śaktijaḥ śaktimānmune
tasmāduttiṣṭha saṃtyajya śokaṃ brahmasutottama //
1.64.d:
मत्समस्तव पौत्रो ऽसौ शक्तिजः शक्तिमान्मुने
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ संत्यज्य शोकं ब्रह्मसुतोत्तम ॥
1.64.m: This grandson of yours, the son of Śakti, is equal to me and possessed of power, O sage; / therefore rise, having cast off grief, O best among the sons of Brahmā!

1.64.s:
rudrabhaktaś ca garbhastho rudrapūjāparāyaṇaḥ
rudradevaprabhāveṇa kulaṃ te saṃtariṣyati //
1.64.d:
रुद्रभक्तश् च गर्भस्थो रुद्रपूजापरायणः
रुद्रदेवप्रभावेण कुलं ते संतरिष्यति ॥
